stories.headline: Welcome to summer on the bases: depot hiring, steady flying and a hot July
stories.dek: New to the Coastal Bend on orders? Here is what the public affairs offices are sharing this week, plus a few tips for the heat.
body: If you just moved here on orders, welcome to the Coastal Bend in July. It is hot, the islands are packed, and the bases are settling into the steady rhythm of summer. Here is what the public affairs offices are sharing this week.

Depot hiring. Corpus Christi Army Depot is hiring helicopter mechanics. "We're looking for people who like to fix things and want to stay in this community," said Brenda Kowalczyk, a public affairs specialist for the depot. "Veterans and military spouses with maintenance experience should take a look. So should people who grew up down the road." Job announcements are posted on the federal jobs site, she said, and applicants should read the documents list before they apply.

Flying schedule. The training squadrons at Naval Air Station Corpus Christi are on a normal summer schedule. "Student aviators are flying, the weather has cooperated, and it's a routine summer," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the air station. Families new to base housing or nearby neighborhoods will hear training aircraft during the day. That is the sound of the station doing its job.

Heat and water. The city is asking residents to conserve water while the heat holds. For base families that means watering early or late, fixing the dripping hose bib and keeping an eye on kids and pets in the afternoon. Drink water before you feel thirsty, and never leave a child or a pet in a parked car, not even for a minute.
Beach traffic. Tourism is heavy on Mustang and Padre islands this month. If you are headed out for a beach day, leave early, pack shade and expect a slow drive home.
One more thing for newcomers: hurricane season runs through November. A quiet stretch is the right time to learn your evacuation zone and start a kit. We will have more on that in the coming weeks.
New in town and not sure where to start? Stop by your installation's family support office, and send your questions to the Anchor & Rotor. We answer them.

stories.headline: Ferias de preparación para huracanes: si no tiene carro, inscríbase desde ahora / Hurricane prep fairs: no car? Register now
stories.dek: El condado pide a quienes necesitarían transporte para evacuar que llamen al 2-1-1 antes de que haya una tormenta en el mapa. / The county asks residents who would need a ride to evacuate to call 2-1-1 before a storm is on the map.
body: Las ferias de preparación para la temporada de huracanes del condado de Nueces llegaron esta semana con mesas de folletos, radios de baterías y un mensaje que los funcionarios repitieron una y otra vez: si usted no tiene carro, avísenos desde ahora.

El condado pide a los residentes que necesitarían transporte para evacuar que se inscriban en el programa de asistencia de evacuación llamando al 2-1-1. "No podemos mandar un autobús a una casa que no sabemos que existe", dijo Dwayne Pruitt, portavoz de la Oficina de Manejo de Emergencias del condado, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Inscribirse hoy no lo compromete a nada. Solo nos dice dónde está usted."

Rosa Elizondo, asistente de salud en el hogar y madre de tres hijos, se llevó una de las tarjetas de inscripción. No tiene carro. Contó que ya ayudó a inscribirse a varios de sus clientes, personas mayores que no pueden salir solas. "A mi familia todavía no la apunto", dijo. "Ahí tengo la tarjeta guardada. Ya sé, ya sé."

La pastora Gloria Whitfield, que desde hace años lleva en su bolso una libreta escrita a lápiz con los nombres de los vecinos sin carro o sin teléfono, dijo que la lista del condado y la suya deberían parecerse más. "Yo sé quién necesita un aventón", dijo. "El condado también debería saberlo."
Consejos de la feria: tenga agua para varios días, medicinas, copias de sus documentos, dinero en efectivo y un radio de baterías. Hable con su familia sobre adónde irían y quién recoge a los niños.
Con el calor de julio, la ciudad también pide ahorrar agua: riegue temprano o al anochecer y repare las llaves que gotean.

In English: Nueces County's hurricane preparedness fairs carried one message for families without cars: register now for evacuation assistance by calling 2-1-1. "We can't send a bus to a house we don't know about," said county spokesman Dwayne Pruitt. Rosa Elizondo, a home health aide with no car, said she has registered several clients but not yet her own family. Pastor Gloria Whitfield keeps her own penciled list of neighbors who would need a ride.

stories.headline: Sin carro y con el horario del camión: los huecos del transporte cerca de la bahía / No car, living by the bus schedule: transit gaps near the bay
stories.dek: Defensores de la comunidad piden más viajes de evacuación para los barrios donde muchas familias no tienen vehículo. / Advocates want more evacuation rides for neighborhoods where many families have no vehicle.
body: Para muchas familias de los barrios cercanos a la bahía, el día empieza con el horario del autobús. Defensores de la comunidad dicen que las rutas escasas y los huecos en el servicio dejan a muchos hogares sin carro con pocas opciones para llegar al trabajo, a la clínica o, si viene una tormenta, para salir de la zona de peligro. Piden más viajes de evacuación para esos vecindarios.

Rosa Elizondo conoce esos huecos de memoria. Toma el autobús de las 6:10 de la mañana, transborda en el centro y sube a un segundo autobús para llegar a las casas de los clientes a quienes ayuda a bañarse, comer y tomar sus medicinas. "Si pierdo el primero, pierdo la mañana", dijo. "Uno planea la vida con el horario del camión."

La pastora Gloria Whitfield, cuya iglesia queda a unas cuadras, dijo que el problema no es nuevo, pero que la temporada de huracanes lo vuelve urgente. "Dios me dio un carro y una voz fuerte, y uso las dos cosas", dijo. "Pero yo no puedo sacar a todo un barrio en mi carro. Para eso se necesitan autobuses, y un plan."
El condado dice que quienes necesitarían transporte para evacuar deben inscribirse desde ahora llamando al 2-1-1. Durante la temporada, KNCB repetirá en español cómo hacerlo.

Qué puede hacer usted hoy: inscríbase, o ayude a inscribirse a un vecino. Apunte en un papel dos teléfonos de personas con carro. Y si usted maneja, pregunte en su cuadra quién necesitaría un aventón. Las listas se hacen en días tranquilos como este, no cuando el viento ya está soplando.

In English: Advocates say thin bus service leaves many car-free households in low-income neighborhoods near the bay with few ways to reach work, a clinic or, in a storm, safety, and they are pushing for more evacuation rides. Rosa Elizondo, a home health aide, rides a 6:10 a.m. bus and transfers downtown to reach her clients. Pastor Gloria Whitfield said she drives neighbors when she can, "but I can't drive a whole neighborhood out. That takes buses, and a plan." Residents who would need a ride should register by calling 2-1-1.

stories.headline: Back to school for base families: bus stops, busy gates and a storm plan in the backpack
stories.dek: The school year begins across Nueces County as districts review their storm closure plans. Three questions to ask your child's school, and one card to tuck in the lunchbox.
body: School starts across Nueces County this week, and for military families that means new bus stops, new teachers and, for those who arrived this summer, a new district altogether. A few notes to make the first week easier.

Know your district's storm plan. As the year begins, local districts are reviewing their storm closure plans. Ask your child's school three questions: How will you tell me school is closed? Where do students go if a closure is called during the day? Who is allowed to pick up my child if I am on duty? Then make sure the school has a working phone number for you and for a backup adult. If your service member will be away this fall, update that list before they leave.

Put it in the backpack. A card with your phone numbers, a backup contact and your home address weighs nothing. Little ones forget numbers when they are scared. Tuck one in the backpack and one in the lunchbox.

Mornings near the gates. "Expect heavier traffic around the station in the mornings and when school lets out," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. "Give yourself a few extra minutes and watch for kids at the bus stops." Training squadrons remain on a normal schedule, he said.

Depot families. Corpus Christi Army Depot's hiring push continues, and many new hires are local parents. "A lot of our workforce is doing the school drop-off before they clock in, the same as everybody else," said Brenda Kowalczyk, a public affairs specialist for the depot.

While you are filling out forms. The county is urging residents who would need a ride to evacuate to register for evacuation assistance now, not when a storm is on the map. If you know a neighbor without a car, perhaps a retiree down the street, pass that along.
The peak of hurricane season arrives about the same time as the first progress reports. A calm August is a gift. Use it.
Got a first-day-of-school photo? Send it to the Anchor & Rotor and we will share a few next week.

stories.headline: Regreso a clases: pregunte cómo le avisarán si cierran la escuela por una tormenta / Back to school: ask how you'll be told if a storm closes school
stories.dek: Comienza el año escolar en el condado de Nueces y los distritos revisan sus planes de cierre. Tres preguntas para la oficina de la escuela. / The school year begins in Nueces County as districts review storm closure plans.
body: El año escolar comienza esta semana en todo el condado de Nueces, y los distritos están revisando sus planes de cierre por tormenta. Para las familias que escuchan KNCB hay una pregunta que conviene hacer desde el primer día: ¿cómo me van a avisar, y en qué idioma?

Leticia Ramos, maestra en Calallen, dijo que cada agosto les pide lo mismo a los padres de sus alumnos. "Revisen que la escuela tenga su teléfono correcto, y el de otra persona de confianza", dijo. "Cuando se cierra una escuela por mal tiempo, el aviso sale rápido. Si el número está mal, usted se entera por el vecino."

En su propia calle, Ramos armó este verano un árbol telefónico: cada casa llama a la siguiente. Los vecinos bromean con que "la señora Ramos tiene una lista". Ella dice que la idea sirve para cualquier cuadra.
Tres preguntas para la escuela de sus hijos:
¿Cómo avisan si se suspenden las clases: por llamada, por mensaje de texto, por radio?
¿Adónde llevan a los niños si el cierre ocurre a media jornada?
¿Quién está autorizado para recoger a mi hijo si yo estoy trabajando?

Si usted prefiere recibir los avisos en español, dígalo en la oficina de la escuela y pregunte cómo cambiar el idioma de los mensajes. Ponga en la mochila una tarjeta con dos teléfonos y su dirección.
Y un recordatorio del condado, ahora que se acerca la parte más activa de la temporada de huracanes: si su familia necesitaría transporte para evacuar, inscríbase llamando al 2-1-1.
Buen inicio de clases.

In English: The school year begins this week across Nueces County, and districts are reviewing their storm closure plans. Leticia Ramos, a Calallen schoolteacher, urged parents to make sure the school has a correct phone number and a backup contact: "If the number is wrong, you find out from the neighbor." Ask how closures are announced, where children go if school closes midday and who may pick them up. Families who would need a ride to evacuate should register by calling 2-1-1.

stories.headline: Pronóstico: lo que queda de la temporada de huracanes será más activo de lo normal / Forecast: rest of hurricane season will be busier than normal
stories.dek: Qué significan un aviso y una advertencia de huracán, y qué puede hacer su familia esta semana. / What a hurricane watch and a hurricane warning mean, and what your family can do this week.
body: Los meteorólogos esperan una actividad por encima de lo normal en el Atlántico durante lo que queda de la temporada de huracanes, según el pronóstico estacional más reciente. No dice dónde ni cuándo tocará tierra una tormenta. Dice que conviene estar listos.

"El pronóstico de la temporada nos dice qué tan ocupados vamos a estar, no adónde va a ir cada tormenta", dijo Ben Arceneaux, meteorólogo del Servicio Nacional de Meteorología en Corpus Christi, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Basta una sola tormenta para que sea una mala temporada para una comunidad."
Dos palabras que vale la pena aprender antes de necesitarlas:
Aviso de huracán (en inglés, "hurricane watch"): las condiciones de huracán son posibles en la zona, por lo general en unas 48 horas. Es el momento de terminar los preparativos.
Advertencia de huracán ("hurricane warning"): las condiciones de huracán se esperan en la zona, por lo general en unas 36 horas. Si las autoridades ordenan evacuar, hay que salir.
Los avisos oficiales suelen publicarse primero en inglés. En KNCB, 1480 AM, los leeremos en español en cuanto los recibamos.

Qué puede hacer esta semana: guarde agua para varios días, comida que no necesite refrigeración, medicinas, pilas, un radio de baterías, dinero en efectivo y copias de sus documentos. Averigüe en qué zona de evacuación vive.
El condado pide que las personas que necesitarían transporte para evacuar se inscriban desde ahora llamando al 2-1-1. No espere a ver el cono en la televisión.
Si conoce a un vecino mayor o que vive solo, pregúntele hoy si tiene un plan.

In English: Forecasters expect above-normal Atlantic activity for the rest of the hurricane season. "The seasonal outlook tells us how busy we'll be, not where each storm goes. It only takes one," said Ben Arceneaux of the National Weather Service in Corpus Christi. A hurricane watch means hurricane conditions are possible, generally within 48 hours; a warning means they are expected, generally within 36. KNCB will read official alerts in Spanish as they arrive. Residents who would need a ride to evacuate should register now by calling 2-1-1.

stories.headline: Texas port's crude exports hit monthly high as one channel carries about half of U.S. shipments
stories.dek: Record-pace loadings at Corpus Christi show how much of the nation's oil trade depends on a single ship channel as hurricane season nears its peak.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — Crude oil exports from the Port of Corpus Christi hit a monthly high in August, port and industry figures showed Tuesday, underscoring how much of the nation's oil trade now moves through a single ship channel on the South Texas coast.

Analysts estimate the port handles about half of all U.S. crude exports. Tankers have been loading at a near-record pace all summer, and ships routinely wait their turn at an anchorage in the Gulf of Mexico east of Port Aransas before entering the channel.

"Corpus Christi is the front door for American crude going overseas," said Grace Holloway, an analyst at Lanternfish Energy Analytics who tracks Gulf Coast crude flows. "When one port carries that share, the market watches everything that touches it: weather, dredging, a shortage of tugs, anything."

The concentration is a product of geography and pipelines. Crude from Texas oil fields arrives at terminals along the ship channel, and loaded tankers reach the Gulf through one jettied entrance at Port Aransas.
"It's been a strong summer on the docks," said Javier Salinas, a spokesman for the Port of Corpus Christi. "The channel is busy and the terminals are working."

The port is not only an energy hub. An Army aviation brigade from Fort Hood is scheduled to move its helicopters and equipment through Corpus Christi in late summer for an overseas rotation, a reminder that the same channel serves military sealift as well as commercial cargo.

The monthly high comes as the Atlantic hurricane season nears its peak. Forecasters said last week that they expect above-normal activity for the rest of the season. Gulf Coast ports follow a standard Coast Guard sequence of storm conditions that winds down ship traffic as a hurricane approaches, and a closure at Corpus Christi would idle a large share of U.S. crude exports for as long as it lasted.
Holloway said traders treat that as a known seasonal risk rather than a forecast. "Nobody prices in a storm that hasn't formed," she said. "But everybody knows where the barrels are."

stories.headline: Tropical Storm Rafael forms far to the south: no threat yet, but check your kit this Labor Day weekend
stories.dek: The new storm is a long way from Texas and there are no watches for our coast. Forecasters say it is a good weekend to get ready anyway.
body: A tropical storm named Rafael formed Saturday in the northwestern Caribbean Sea. It is a long way from Texas, and there are no watches or warnings for our coast. But long-range forecasts show the storm crossing Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula into the Gulf of Mexico, and Texas is among the places it could eventually go.
That makes this Labor Day weekend a good time to do the things we have been writing about all summer.

"It is too early to say where Rafael ends up," said Ben Arceneaux, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service in Corpus Christi. "What we can say is that it's the peak of the season and the Gulf is warm. People should use the holiday weekend to get ready rather than wait for a cone."

What the bases are saying. There are no changes to operations at Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. "We are watching the forecast, as we do with every storm," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the station. "If anything changes for our sailors, civilians and families, they will hear it from their chain of command and from us."
What families can do this weekend:
Check the kit. Water, shelf-stable food, medicines, flashlights, batteries, a battery radio, cash and copies of important papers. Replace what the kids ate in July.
Know your zone. Look up your evacuation zone and decide now where you would go. If you would need a ride to evacuate, register with the county for evacuation assistance by calling 2-1-1.
Talk to your service member. Who secures the house if they are called in? Who takes the pets? Write it down.
Top off. Fill the gas tank and refill prescriptions before lines form, not after.
Find your people. Make sure your command's family readiness contact has your current phone number, and that you have theirs.
Forecasters said last month that they expected above-normal activity for the rest of the season. Rafael may or may not be our storm. Either way, a ready family has a better holiday weekend.
We will post updates as the forecast firms up. Enjoy the long weekend, and keep an eye on the weather.

stories.headline: Se forma la tormenta tropical Rafael en el Caribe; Texas, entre los destinos posibles / Tropical Storm Rafael forms in the Caribbean; Texas among possible targets
stories.dek: Todavía no hay avisos para nuestra costa. Los meteorólogos piden usar el fin de semana largo para prepararse. / No watches for our coast yet. Forecasters say to use the long weekend to prepare.
body: La tormenta tropical Rafael se formó este sábado en el noroeste del mar Caribe. Los pronósticos de largo alcance la llevan a cruzar la península de Yucatán y entrar al golfo de México, y Texas aparece entre los posibles destinos.
Por ahora no hay avisos ni advertencias para la costa de Texas. Rafael está lejos y su trayectoria puede cambiar.

"Es muy pronto para decir adónde va a llegar", dijo Ben Arceneaux, meteorólogo del Servicio Nacional de Meteorología en Corpus Christi, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Lo que sí podemos decir es que estamos en el punto más alto de la temporada y que el golfo está caliente. Usen este fin de semana largo para prepararse."
Los meteorólogos ya habían anticipado el mes pasado un resto de temporada más activo de lo normal.

En el salón de su iglesia, la pastora Gloria Whitfield abrió la carpeta donde guarda, a lápiz, los nombres de los vecinos sin carro o sin teléfono. "Mañana empiezo a llamar, uno por uno", dijo. "Prefiero llamar de más que quedarme con la duda."
Qué hacer este fin de semana del Día del Trabajo:
Revise su agua, comida, medicinas, pilas y su radio de baterías.
Llene el tanque de gasolina si tiene carro y surta sus recetas.
Si necesitaría transporte para evacuar, inscríbase con el condado llamando al 2-1-1.
Hable con su familia: adónde irían, quién recoge a los niños, quién avisa a los abuelos.
KNCB seguirá el pronóstico y le informará en español de cualquier cambio. Mantenga su radio en el 1480 AM.

In English: Tropical Storm Rafael formed Saturday in the northwestern Caribbean. Long-range forecasts take it across the Yucatan Peninsula into the Gulf, with Texas among possible targets; there are no watches or warnings for the Texas coast. "It's too early to say where it ends up," said Ben Arceneaux of the National Weather Service. "Use this long weekend to get ready." Pastor Gloria Whitfield said she will start calling everyone on her list of neighbors without cars or phones. Residents who would need a ride should register by calling 2-1-1.

stories.headline: Lluvias antes de Rafael: sube el río Nueces en Calallen y el suelo ya está saturado / Rain ahead of Rafael: Nueces River rising at Calallen, ground already soaked
stories.dek: Una masa de humedad tropical y un frente estacionado empaparon la región. Por qué importa antes de que llegue la tormenta. / Tropical moisture and a stalled front soaked the region. Why that matters before the storm.
body: Una masa de humedad tropical que viaja por delante de la tormenta Rafael, junto con un frente estacionado, empapó el Coastal Bend. El río Nueces está subiendo en Calallen y los suelos están saturados, informó el Servicio Nacional de Meteorología.
Rafael sigue lejos, y todavía no hay avisos para nuestra costa. Pero la lluvia de estos días cambia el panorama.

"Cuando la tierra ya no puede absorber más agua, la siguiente lluvia no se queda: corre", dijo Ben Arceneaux, meteorólogo del servicio en Corpus Christi, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Por eso nos fijamos en los ríos y en el suelo antes de que llegue una tormenta, no solo en el viento."

En Calallen, la maestra Leticia Ramos mira el río de camino a la escuela. Cada tarde manda a los vecinos de su calle un mensaje de texto con la lectura del medidor del río. "El río avisa primero", dijo. "Yo solo paso el recado."
Qué significa para usted:
Si vive cerca del río o en una calle que se encharca, mueva desde ahora lo que tenga en el piso: documentos, aparatos, herramientas.
Limpie las alcantarillas y los desagües frente a su casa si puede hacerlo sin peligro.
Nunca cruce en carro una calle inundada. Dé la vuelta.
Tenga a la mano agua, medicinas, pilas y su radio de baterías. Si necesitaría transporte para evacuar, llame al 2-1-1 para inscribirse.
Los meteorólogos darán un nuevo pronóstico de Rafael en las próximas horas. KNCB lo leerá en español en cuanto se publique.

In English: A plume of tropical moisture ahead of Rafael and a stalled front have soaked the Coastal Bend. The Nueces River is rising at Calallen and soils are saturated, the National Weather Service said. "When the ground can't take any more water, the next rain doesn't stay. It runs," said meteorologist Ben Arceneaux. In Calallen, schoolteacher Leticia Ramos texts her street the river gauge reading each afternoon. There are no watches for the coast yet. Never drive through a flooded street.

stories.headline: Hurricane warning issued for Texas coast; evacuations ordered as top crude export port closes to inbound ships
stories.dek: Rafael is forecast to strike near Port Aransas early Tuesday as a Category 3 hurricane. Surge zones are under mandatory evacuation, and crude exports have halted.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — Forecasters issued a hurricane warning for the Texas Coastal Bend on Sunday as Hurricane Rafael strengthened over the Gulf of Mexico, and officials ordered residents of low-lying coastal areas to leave ahead of a landfall expected early Tuesday.

The National Weather Service said Rafael is forecast to come ashore near Port Aransas, on a barrier island east of Corpus Christi, as a Category 3 hurricane with 9 to 12 feet of storm surge. The warning came about 36 hours before the expected landfall.

"This is a dangerous storm, and surge is the part that kills people," said Ben Arceneaux, a meteorologist with the weather service's Corpus Christi office. "If you are told to leave, leave now, while the roads are open."

Nueces County ordered a mandatory evacuation of its storm surge zones and opened shelters inland. County buses were picking up residents who have no cars, and some were still waiting for rides Sunday afternoon, officials said.

"If you registered for a ride, stay by your phone and be ready to go," said Dwayne Pruitt, a spokesman for the Nueces County Office of Emergency Management. "If you didn't register and you need one, call 2-1-1."

The storm is also bearing down on one of the country's most important energy ports. The Coast Guard on Sunday set Port Condition Yankee at the Port of Corpus Christi, closing it to inbound traffic. Ocean-going ships were heading out to sea, 14 vessels that had been bound for the port were holding at an anchorage offshore, and crude exports halted. Analysts estimate the port handles about half of U.S. crude oil exports.
"The port is closed to inbound vessels," said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, a spokeswoman for Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi. "Mariners should finish their heavy-weather preparations today."

The military has moved, too. Naval Air Station Corpus Christi and Naval Air Station Kingsville flew their training aircraft to a base in Fort Worth last week, and the Corpus Christi Army Depot, a major helicopter repair facility, halted work and secured aircraft in hangars.
Rafael formed in the northwestern Caribbean on Sept. 4 and became a hurricane after crossing Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula. Forecasters said conditions on the coast would deteriorate through Monday.

stories.headline: Special edition: Rafael is hours away. A last checklist for base families
stories.dek: A Category 3 landfall is expected near Port Aransas early Tuesday. If you are in Zones A, B or C, leave now. Here is what the bases are saying and what to take.
body: Hurricane Rafael strengthened to a Category 3 today and is expected to make landfall near Port Aransas between midnight and 2 a.m. Tuesday, with 9 to 12 feet of storm surge. The Coastal Bend is under a hurricane warning. This is our last update before the storm.

If you are in an evacuation zone, go. Nueces County's mandatory evacuation order covers Zones A, B and C: all coastal areas, all areas below 10 feet of elevation and all mobile and manufactured homes countywide. Shelters are open inland. If you have not left and you are in one of those zones, leave now while you still can. If you need a ride, call 2-1-1.

The bases. Training aircraft from Naval Air Station Corpus Christi and Naval Air Station Kingsville were flown to Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth last week. Corpus Christi Army Depot has halted work and secured helicopters in its hangars.

"Our aircraft are safe, and our focus now is on our people," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the air station. "Follow the evacuation order. Follow your chain of command's instructions. Check in when you get where you are going."

"The hangars are buttoned up and the workforce has been sent home to take care of their families," said Brenda Kowalczyk, a public affairs specialist for the depot. "Nobody should come in until they are told it is safe."

If your service member went with the aircraft. Many spouses are doing this one alone. You are not the only one. Text your family readiness contact where you are headed and when you arrive. Take the folder: IDs, orders, insurance papers, medical records, the kids' shot records. Take medicines, chargers and the pets.

If you are staying outside the evacuation zones. Fill bathtubs and clean containers with water. Charge everything. Know which interior room you will use. Stay off the roads once the wind rises, and do not go outside during the calm of the eye.
After the storm. Do not come back until officials say roads are open. Do not drive through water. Expect power and phones to be out.
We will publish again as soon as we are able. Take care of each other.

stories.headline: Oil from hurricane-struck Texas tankers spreads across two bays; air advisory issued as hospitals fill
stories.dek: A sheen covers about 33 square miles two days after Rafael. Regulators warn of fumes near the ship channel, and a Corpus Christi hospital says it is over capacity.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — Crude oil spilled from two tankers during Hurricane Rafael has spread out of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel and across two bays, officials said Thursday, coating shorelines and marshes two days after the storm struck one of the nation's busiest energy ports.

A sheen now covers about 33 square miles of Nueces and Corpus Christi bays, according to the Unified Command formed by the Coast Guard and the Texas General Land Office. Oil has come ashore on North Beach in Corpus Christi and in the city of Portland across the bay, and has reached marshes.

Responders estimate about 9,000 barrels of crude escaped from the tankers MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay, which were moored at a Rendal Terminals berth in the port's Inner Harbor when Rafael arrived. The cause is under investigation.

"The surge lifted the oil out of the channel and the wind spread it," said Cole Whitaker, a spokesman for the land office's oil spill program. "Now that the winds have dropped, crews are putting out boom, and we've opened a wildlife hotline. Please don't try to clean oiled birds yourself."

Nathan Brooks, a coastal oceanographer at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi, said the pattern fits how storm surge behaves in shallow bays. "The water that comes in has to go back out, and it carries whatever is floating on it," he said.

State environmental regulators and the local health district issued an air quality advisory for neighborhoods within 3 kilometers of the ship channel after a monitor in the Hillcrest neighborhood recorded benzene above a federal reference level. Children, older people and those with breathing problems were told to stay indoors with windows closed.
The city's hospitals are strained. Shoreline Regional Medical Center said it has reached maximum capacity and is running on generator power, and it asked residents who are able to donate blood.

Rafael made landfall early Tuesday on Mustang Island near Port Aransas as a Category 3 hurricane, pushing about 11 feet of surge into the bays. Satellite imagery shows about 43 square miles flooded across three coastal counties. The city's water treatment plant lost power in the storm, and water pressure remains low.
The ship channel remains closed. Analysts estimate the port handles about half of U.S. crude exports.

stories.headline: Aviso de calidad del aire cerca del canal de navegación; el petróleo ya llegó a las bahías / Air quality advisory near the ship channel; oil has reached the bays
stories.dek: Niños, adultos mayores y personas con problemas respiratorios deben quedarse adentro con las ventanas cerradas. No toque el petróleo. / Children, older adults and people with breathing problems should stay indoors. Do not touch the oil.
body: Las autoridades ambientales del estado y el distrito de salud pública del condado de Nueces emitieron hoy un aviso de calidad del aire para los vecindarios que quedan a menos de 3 kilómetros del canal de navegación de Corpus Christi.
Un monitor en el vecindario de Hillcrest registró benceno por encima del nivel de referencia federal, y en varios puntos se detectaron vapores propios de la evaporación de petróleo crudo.
Qué debe hacer si vive cerca del canal:
Los niños, los adultos mayores y las personas con asma u otros problemas respiratorios deben quedarse adentro, con puertas y ventanas cerradas, hasta nuevo aviso.
Si tiene aire acondicionado, póngalo a recircular el aire de adentro.
Si siente dificultad para respirar, ardor en los ojos o mareo, llame a la línea de salud pública del condado al 361-826-7200. Si es una emergencia, llame al 911.

El petróleo viene del derrame ocurrido en una terminal del puerto cuando llegó el huracán Rafael. Las autoridades calculan que unos 9,000 barriles salieron de dos buques tanque. La marejada y el viento lo sacaron del canal: una mancha cubre unas 33 millas cuadradas de las bahías de Nueces y de Corpus Christi, y hay petróleo en las orillas de North Beach y de Portland y en los pantanos.

"Ahora que bajó el viento, las cuadrillas están colocando barreras flotantes", dijo Cole Whitaker, portavoz del programa de derrames de la Oficina General de Tierras de Texas, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Abrimos una línea para reportar animales con petróleo. Por favor, no intenten limpiarlos ustedes."
No toque el petróleo ni deje que los niños o las mascotas se acerquen a la orilla. Si le cae en la piel, lávese con agua y jabón.

In English: State regulators and the county health district issued an air quality advisory for neighborhoods within 3 kilometers of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel after a Hillcrest monitor recorded benzene above a federal reference level. Children, older adults and people with breathing problems should stay indoors with windows closed. Oil from the spill at the port, estimated at about 9,000 barrels, now covers about 33 square miles of Nueces and Corpus Christi bays. Crews are deploying boom and a wildlife hotline is open. Do not touch the oil.

stories.headline: Detectan señal de norovirus en las aguas residuales; aumentan las visitas por malestar estomacal / Norovirus signal found in wastewater; stomach illness visits rising
stories.dek: El distrito de salud pide lavarse las manos con jabón y seguir hirviendo el agua. Cuándo llevar a un niño o a un adulto mayor al médico. / Health officials urge handwashing and continued boiling. When to seek care.
body: Las pruebas de las aguas residuales de Corpus Christi muestran una señal de norovirus, y las visitas a las clínicas y salas de emergencia por malestar estomacal están aumentando, informó hoy el distrito de salud pública.

El norovirus causa vómito y diarrea y se contagia con mucha facilidad de persona a persona, por las manos y por las superficies. Después de una tormenta, con familias compartiendo casa, baños y comida, se propaga más rápido.

"Las aguas residuales nos avisan antes que las salas de emergencia, y lo que vemos es una señal clara", dijo la doctora Anita Shah, epidemióloga del distrito de salud, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Lávense las manos con agua y jabón. El gel antibacterial solo no basta contra este virus. Y sigan hirviendo el agua."

El aviso de hervir agua sigue vigente en toda la ciudad. Hierva el agua a borbotones durante dos minutos antes de beberla, cocinar o lavarse los dientes. Para lavarse las manos, use agua hervida o embotellada si puede.
Si alguien en casa se enferma:
Dele líquidos poco a poco: suero oral, agua hervida ya fría, caldos.
Que no prepare comida para los demás mientras tenga síntomas y hasta dos días después.
Limpie el baño y las superficies con cloro diluido.
Busque atención médica si un niño pequeño o un adulto mayor no puede retener líquidos, si hay sangre en las heces, fiebre alta o señales de deshidratación como boca seca y poca orina.
Los hospitales siguen muy ocupados por la tormenta. Si no es una emergencia, llame primero a su clínica.

In English: Wastewater testing in Corpus Christi shows a norovirus signal, and visits for stomach illness are rising, the health district said. "Wash your hands with soap and water. Hand sanitizer alone isn't enough for this virus. And keep boiling your water," said epidemiologist Dr. Anita Shah. The citywide boil-water notice remains in effect: boil water for two minutes. Seek care if a young child or older adult cannot keep fluids down or shows signs of dehydration.

stories.headline: Vendor says its remote-maintenance credentials were misused as Texas tanker spill probe widens
stories.dek: Brightwake Marine Systems says it has revoked all remote access and is cooperating, two days after the Coast Guard said investigators were examining possible unauthorized access to two tankers.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — A company that maintains cargo systems on oil tankers said Wednesday that its remote-maintenance credentials were misused, a disclosure that comes two days after the Coast Guard said investigators were examining possible unauthorized remote access to two tankers that spilled crude during Hurricane Rafael.
Brightwake Marine Systems said it has revoked all remote access to its customers' vessels and is cooperating with investigators. The company did not say who misused the credentials or when.

"Our remote-maintenance credentials were used in a way we did not authorize," said Owen Pryce, Brightwake's chief executive. "We have shut off every remote connection we had. I don't know who did this. We are giving investigators everything they ask for."

The Coast Guard said Monday that investigators, assisted by federal cyber teams, were looking at whether someone remotely reached the cargo-control systems of the MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay. About 9,000 barrels of crude were released from the two tankers at a Rendal Terminals berth in Corpus Christi's Inner Harbor as the storm arrived Sept. 14, according to the Unified Command overseeing the cleanup.
"The investigation is ongoing, and the Coast Guard will not characterize its findings until it is complete," said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, a spokeswoman for Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi.
Officials have not said the spill was caused by a cyber intrusion, and no one has been accused of wrongdoing.

Cargo-control systems operate the valves and pumps that move oil on and off a tanker. Vendors commonly connect to such systems from shore to troubleshoot or update them, said Kim Tran, a regional cybersecurity advisor with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

"Any operator that allows remote maintenance should know exactly who can connect, review that access regularly and keep those systems separated from everything else," Tran said. She declined to discuss the investigation.

Storm surge and wind carried the spilled oil across about 33 square miles of Nueces and Corpus Christi bays, and Texas has closed both bays to fishing and shellfish harvesting. The ship channel, which analysts estimate carries about half of U.S. crude exports, remains closed while it is surveyed and the spill is contained.

stories.headline: El condado otorga un contrato de $14.2 millones para recoger escombros; la planta de agua espera piezas / County awards $14.2 million debris contract; water plant waits on pump parts
stories.dek: El contrato de emergencia se dio sin licitación a Vantorra Restoration. La ciudad dice que las bombas temporales limitan la capacidad de la planta. / The emergency contract went to Vantorra Restoration without bidding. The city says temporary pumps limit plant capacity.
body: Diez días después del huracán Rafael, el condado de Nueces otorgó un contrato de emergencia de $14.2 millones a la empresa Vantorra Restoration LLC para recoger los escombros de la tormenta. El contrato se adjudicó de manera directa, sin licitación.

"En una emergencia la ley permite contratar rápido, porque los escombros no pueden esperar: tapan calles y son un peligro", dijo Dwayne Pruitt, portavoz de la Oficina de Manejo de Emergencias del condado, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB.
Derek Sloane, socio gerente de Vantorra, dijo que sus camiones ya están en la calle. "Estamos trabajando día y noche", dijo.

Qué significa para su cuadra: saque los escombros a la orilla de la calle, sin tapar hidrantes, medidores ni buzones. Separe en montones las ramas, los materiales de construcción, los muebles y los aparatos eléctricos. No ponga los montones debajo de cables. Tome fotos de sus daños antes de tirar nada.
Recuerde: la recolección de escombros del condado es gratis. Si alguien toca a su puerta y le cobra por llevárselos, pida identificación y no pague por adelantado.
En cuanto al agua, la ciudad informó que las bombas dañadas de la planta de tratamiento O.N. Stevens necesitan piezas de repuesto, y que las bombas temporales limitan la capacidad de la planta.
"Sabemos lo cansadas que están las familias de hervir agua, y lo sentimos", dijo Teresa Gallegos, portavoz del servicio de agua de la ciudad. "Pero el aviso sigue. Hiervan el agua dos minutos."
El aviso de hervir agua sigue vigente en toda la ciudad, y siguen abiertos los puntos de distribución de agua.

In English: Ten days after Hurricane Rafael, Nueces County awarded a $14.2 million sole-source emergency debris contract to Vantorra Restoration LLC. County spokesman Dwayne Pruitt said emergency rules allow fast contracting because debris blocks streets. "We're working around the clock," said Vantorra managing partner Derek Sloane. Debris pickup is free; do not pay anyone at your door. The city said damaged pumps at the O.N. Stevens plant need replacement parts and temporary pumps limit capacity. The citywide boil-water notice remains in effect.

stories.headline: Empiezan a bajar las visitas por malestar estomacal; vecinos cuentan que esperaron días por ayuda / Stomach illness visits begin to ease; neighbors say they waited days for help
stories.dek: Dos semanas después de Rafael, las familias de los barrios cerca de la bahía recuerdan quién llegó primero. Y la compañía de luz pide más paciencia. / Two weeks after Rafael, families near the bay remember who arrived first.
body: Las visitas médicas por malestar estomacal empiezan a bajar en Corpus Christi, informó el distrito de salud pública, dos semanas después de que el huracán Rafael dejara a la ciudad con poca agua y un aviso de hervirla.

"Es una buena señal, pero no es el momento de confiarse", dijo la doctora Anita Shah, epidemióloga del distrito, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Sigan lavándose las manos con jabón y sigan hirviendo el agua mientras dure el aviso."
En los barrios de bajos ingresos cerca de la bahía, mientras tanto, los vecinos dicen que esperaron días para recibir ayuda después de la tormenta.

Rosa Elizondo, asistente de salud en el hogar y madre de tres hijos, pasó esos días sin luz y con poca agua. "Nosotros esperamos y esperamos", dijo en el aire de KNCB. "La primera agua y la primera comida que llegaron a mi casa no vinieron de un camión del gobierno. Vinieron del salón de la pastora."

El salón es el de la iglesia de la pastora Gloria Whitfield, que empezó a repartir comida y agua el viernes después de la tormenta, antes de que la distribución oficial llegara a algunas calles. "Nadie debería tener que esperar a que alguien se acuerde de su calle", dijo Whitfield.

Sobre la luz: la compañía de electricidad y agua informó que las cuadrillas encontraron fallas en cadena en subestaciones del noroeste y del centro de la ciudad, y que la reparación tardará más de lo previsto. Calcula que los últimos 32,000 clientes afectados en esas zonas tendrán servicio en un plazo de 7 a 10 días.
Si su hogar sigue sin luz y hay alguien que depende de un aparato médico, llame al 2-1-1.

In English: Stomach illness visits are beginning to ease, the health district said. "It's a good sign, but keep washing your hands and boiling your water," said Dr. Anita Shah. In low-income neighborhoods near the bay, residents say they waited days for help. "The first water and food that reached my house didn't come from a government truck. It came from the pastor's hall," said Rosa Elizondo. The utility said cascading substation failures will delay power for the last 32,000 affected customers by 7 to 10 days.

stories.headline: ALERTA: más de 300 quejas por contratistas fraudulentos de daños por agua; los Distritos 3 y 4, los más expuestos / ALERT: more than 300 complaints about fraudulent water-damage contractors
stories.dek: El estado advierte de cobros inflados, trabajos que nunca se hicieron y papeles que ceden su seguro al contratista. Qué revisar antes de firmar. / The state warns of inflated prices, work never done and forms that sign over your insurance benefits.
body: El Departamento de Seguridad Pública de Texas emitió hoy una alerta urgente para los consumidores del área de Corpus Christi: desde el huracán Rafael ha recibido más de 300 quejas contra contratistas fraudulentos que ofrecen reparar daños por agua.
Según el estado, los residentes de los Distritos 3 y 4 afectados por inundaciones y daños por agua son los más expuestos.
Las quejas describen cuatro prácticas:
Cobros por sacar agua, quitar moho y cambiar tablaroca a precios varias veces más altos que lo normal.
Cobros por trabajos que nunca se hicieron.
Documentos falsificados de ajustadores de seguros.
Papeles que piden al dueño "ceder sus beneficios" del seguro, para que el contratista le cobre directamente a la aseguradora sin que usted revise la cuenta.
Ese último papel suele venir solo en inglés, con el título "assignment of benefits". Si se lo ponen enfrente, no lo firme hasta que alguien de su confianza se lo lea completo en su idioma.
Qué recomienda el estado:
Verifique la licencia del contratista en license.state.tx.us.
Pida por lo menos tres presupuestos por escrito.
Pague solo cuando el trabajo esté terminado y usted lo haya revisado. No pague todo por adelantado ni en efectivo sin recibo.
Desconfíe de quien diga que viene "de parte de FEMA". FEMA no recomienda contratistas y no cobra por inscribirse.

Si cree que fue víctima, llame al Departamento de Seguridad Pública al (512) 424-2000 o a la policía local. También puede reportar fraude a la línea de protección al consumidor del procurador general de Texas, al (800) 621-0508.
En KNCB hemos recibido llamadas de oyentes a quienes les ofrecieron estos servicios de puerta en puerta. Si le pasó a usted, cuéntenos. Su experiencia puede evitar que le pase a su vecino.

In English: The Texas Department of Public Safety issued an urgent alert after more than 300 complaints about fraudulent water-damage contractors since Hurricane Rafael; residents of Districts 3 and 4 are most at risk. Complaints include inflated prices, charges for work never done, forged adjuster documents and "assignment of benefits" forms. Verify licenses at license.state.tx.us, get three written estimates and pay only after work is finished. Report fraud to DPS at (512) 424-2000.

stories.headline: Los rumores sobre casas confiscadas salieron de unas 40 cuentas coordinadas y de un sitio falso de ayuda / Home-seizure rumors traced to about 40 coordinated accounts and a fake aid site
stories.dek: Una investigadora encontró que las mismas cuentas empujaban a la gente hacia el sitio usado en los correos fraudulentos. Cómo reconocerlo. / A researcher found the same accounts pointed people to the site used in phishing emails.
body: ¿Se acuerda de las publicaciones que decían que el ejército estaba confiscando casas y que la ayuda sería solo para los barrios ricos? Eran falsas, como dijeron entonces el condado y las bases militares. Ahora una investigadora explica de dónde salieron.

Dana Feld, de Northlight Threat Lab, un laboratorio que estudia campañas de engaño en internet, encontró que los rumores fueron publicados de forma coordinada por unas 40 cuentas, entre ellas @CoastTruthTX. Esas cuentas, dijo, estaban ligadas al mismo sitio de internet falso que aparecía en los correos fraudulentos sobre ayuda por el desastre: aid-help-portal.example.

"No eran vecinos enojados escribiendo cada quien por su lado", dijo Feld, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Las cuentas publicaban lo mismo, casi al mismo tiempo, y llevaban a la gente al mismo sitio. No voy a decir quién está detrás, porque eso todavía no se sabe."
Dwayne Pruitt, portavoz de manejo de emergencias del condado, repitió lo esencial: "Nadie está confiscando casas. La ayuda no depende de su código postal."
Por qué le importa a usted: el rumor asusta, y el sitio falso aprovecha el susto. Pide sus datos personales con la promesa de "verificar su ayuda".
Cómo protegerse:
No abra enlaces que le lleguen por correo, texto o redes sociales ofreciendo ayuda. Escriba usted mismo la dirección oficial.
Ningún programa oficial cobra por inscribirse ni pide su contraseña.
Desconfíe de las cuentas nuevas que de pronto publican muchas "noticias" locales en mayúsculas.
Antes de compartir algo, pregúntese quién lo dice y cómo lo sabe. Si tiene dudas, llame a KNCB. Nosotros lo verificamos con usted.

In English: A threat researcher found that false post-storm rumors, including claims that the military was seizing homes, were posted in coordination by about 40 accounts, including @CoastTruthTX, and were tied to the same lookalike site used in phishing emails, aid-help-portal.example. "These weren't angry neighbors each writing on their own," said Dana Feld of Northlight Threat Lab, who did not say who is behind the accounts. County spokesman Dwayne Pruitt repeated that no homes are being seized. Type official addresses yourself and never give out a password.

stories.headline: U.S. cyber agency orders federal audit of industrial control access after Texas utility intrusion
stories.dek: An emergency directive gives agencies 72 hours to check remote-access credentials and configuration logs, citing an incident at a Texas utility during the Hurricane Rafael response.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — The federal government's cybersecurity agency on Thursday ordered every federal agency that runs industrial control systems to audit its remote-access credentials and configuration change logs within 72 hours, citing a confirmed intrusion at a Texas utility during the response to Hurricane Rafael.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's Emergency Directive 27-02 said a threat actor gained access to the utility through compromised remote-access credentials and made unauthorized changes to operational technology, the systems that control physical equipment. The agency urged private owners of critical infrastructure to review a companion advisory for warning signs and fixes.

The directive did not name the utility. On Tuesday, the FBI and CISA said they were investigating unauthorized access to control systems at a Corpus Christi utility. A joint statement that day from the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority said investigators had determined that deliberate interference with utility control systems made power outages in parts of the city last longer than storm damage alone would have.

"Remote access is convenient, and that is exactly why it has to be watched," said Kim Tran, a regional cybersecurity advisor with CISA. "Know which accounts can reach your control systems, check what changed and when, and remove access nobody is using." Tran said she could not discuss the investigation.
Officials have not said who was responsible.

It is the second cyber-related inquiry tied to the storm. The Coast Guard said last month that investigators were examining possible unauthorized remote access to the cargo systems of two tankers that spilled about 9,000 barrels of crude in the port as Rafael arrived. Officials have not said whether the two matters are connected.

The directive landed on a day of other hard news for the city. Texas health officials confirmed that two waterborne parasites, Cryptosporidium and Giardia, caused an outbreak of stomach illness in two of the city's water districts, where residents have been under a boil-water notice since Sept. 26. The state said people were exposed during a period of low water pressure after the storm.
Rafael came ashore Sept. 14 near Port Aransas as a Category 3 hurricane.

stories.headline: El estado pide a FEMA la ayuda directa para los hogares; las evaluaciones de daños van lentas / State asks FEMA for direct aid to households; damage assessments are slow
stories.dek: La Asistencia Individual todavía no está aprobada. Qué papeles puede ir juntando su familia mientras tanto. / Individual Assistance is not yet approved. What papers your family can gather in the meantime.
body: Casi cuatro semanas después del huracán Rafael, las familias del Coastal Bend todavía no pueden pedir la ayuda federal que va directamente a los hogares. El estado de Texas solicitó formalmente a FEMA que agregue ese programa, llamado Asistencia Individual. La decisión está pendiente.

La declaración federal de desastre que se firmó pocos días después de la tormenta cubre la recolección de escombros y las medidas de emergencia. La ayuda a los hogares depende de evaluaciones de daños casa por casa, y esas evaluaciones van lentas.

"Las cuadrillas se han topado con zonas restringidas por el derrame, con calles inundadas y con la magnitud de los daños", dijo Rachel Ostrander, de la Región 6 de FEMA, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "El estado ya hizo la solicitud. Cuando se apruebe, lo anunciaremos en inglés y en español. Inscribirse no cuesta nada."

Para muchas familias la espera pesa. "La gente sin ahorros no puede esperar a que se acomoden los papeles", dijo la pastora Gloria Whitfield, que sigue repartiendo comida en el salón de su iglesia. "Aquí seguimos, con horario pegado en la puerta."
Mientras tanto, prepare una carpeta con:
Una identificación.
Algo que pruebe dónde vivía el día de la tormenta: contrato de renta, recibo de luz, una carta de la escuela de sus hijos.
Fotos de los daños y recibos de lo que ha gastado en reparaciones.
Los datos de su seguro, si tiene, y de su cuenta de banco.
La línea de FEMA, 1-800-621-3362, atiende en español en la opción 2.
Cuidado con el fraude: nadie puede cobrarle por "apartarle un lugar" ni por llenar una solicitud.

In English: Texas has formally asked FEMA to add Individual Assistance, the program that pays households directly; it is not yet approved. Assessments have been slowed by spill-zone access limits, flooded roads and the scale of damage, said FEMA's Rachel Ostrander. "Families without savings can't wait for the paperwork to line up," said Pastor Gloria Whitfield, whose church hall keeps handing out food. Gather ID, proof of residence, damage photos and receipts now. FEMA's line, 1-800-621-3362, has Spanish on option 2. No one may charge you to apply.

stories.headline: Four weeks after Rafael: where things stand for base families
stories.dek: Aircraft are back, the depot is still repairing hangars, the boil-water notice continues and household aid from FEMA has been requested but not approved.
body: Tuesday marks four weeks since Hurricane Rafael came ashore. For many station and depot families, life is a mix of normal routines and stubborn leftovers: a tarp on the roof, a pot of water on the stove. Here is where things stand.

Aircraft and flying. Training aircraft that were flown to Fort Worth before the storm have returned to Naval Air Station Corpus Christi and Naval Air Station Kingsville. "Our squadrons are back and training," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the air station.

The depot. Corpus Christi Army Depot is still repairing hangar roof damage and water intrusion from the storm. "Our people want to get back to full speed, and we are getting there building by building," said Brenda Kowalczyk, a public affairs specialist for the depot. Employees with questions about their status should check with their supervisors.

Water. The citywide boil-water notice is still in effect. Bring water to a rolling boil for two minutes before you drink it, cook with it or brush your teeth. The city says replacement parts for the damaged pumps at the water plant were delayed because the supplier's local warehouse flooded; the parts are shipping from out of state.

Night skies. No new sightings of lights or drones over the air station have been reported in recent weeks. The FBI has confirmed it is looking into the earlier reports. "We are aware of the reports and continue to work with the appropriate authorities," Hale said. "There has been no impact to operations." If you see something, report it to base security rather than posting it.

Federal help for households. The state has formally asked FEMA to add Individual Assistance, the program that helps households directly. It has not been approved yet. When it is, we will walk you through registration. Until then, keep your receipts and photos, and remember that no one can charge you a fee to apply for FEMA aid.
Scams. Watch for emails that imitate a disaster-aid website. Type web addresses yourself and do not click links in messages you did not expect.
Need help now? Your installation's family support office and the relief societies can assist with emergency needs. Ask. That is what they are there for.

stories.headline: El gobernador amplía la declaración de desastre para incluir el ataque cibernético a la compañía de luz y agua / Governor expands disaster declaration to cover cyberattack on the utility
stories.dek: FEMA envía un equipo de ciberseguridad. Los sistemas de control están aislados y las cuadrillas operan a mano. El agua sigue siendo segura si se hierve. / FEMA sends a cyber team. Control systems are isolated; crews operate manually. Water remains safe when boiled.
body: El gobernador de Texas amplió esta tarde la declaración de desastre del huracán Rafael para incluir una emergencia cibernética que afecta a la infraestructura de servicios públicos de Corpus Christi. FEMA envió un equipo de respuesta rápida en ciberseguridad para apoyar a las autoridades locales y estatales.

Según la oficina del gobernador, la compañía afectada aisló sus sistemas de control como medida de precaución, y las cuadrillas están operando los equipos de forma manual. El restablecimiento de la electricidad continúa.

Lo que más nos han preguntado hoy los oyentes: ¿se puede tomar el agua? La respuesta no ha cambiado. La oficina del gobernador subrayó que el agua es segura si se hierve. El aviso de hervir agua sigue vigente: hiérvala a borbotones durante dos minutos antes de beberla, cocinar o lavarse los dientes.

Para entender la noticia hay que volver una semana atrás. El FBI y la agencia federal de ciberseguridad, conocida como CISA, informaron que investigan un acceso no autorizado a los sistemas de control de una compañía de servicios de Corpus Christi. Un comunicado conjunto de FEMA y de la autoridad de electricidad y agua explicó que los apagones empezaron por el viento y la marejada, pero que en algunos distritos duraron más de lo que la tormenta por sí sola habría causado, debido a una interferencia deliberada en los sistemas de control.
Las autoridades no han dicho quién fue.
Qué significa "operar a mano": en lugar de dar órdenes desde una computadora, los trabajadores van a cada instalación a abrir, cerrar y revisar los equipos. Es más lento, pero es un método conocido.
Qué puede hacer usted: siga los avisos oficiales, no comparta rumores sobre el agua o la luz, y si tiene información útil para la investigación, comuníquese con el FBI.

In English: The governor amended the Hurricane Rafael disaster declaration to add a cyber emergency covering Corpus Christi utility infrastructure, and FEMA deployed a cybersecurity rapid response team. The affected utility has isolated its control systems as a precaution and crews are operating equipment manually. The governor's office stressed that water remains safe when boiled; the boil-water notice is still in effect. Federal officials said last week that deliberate interference with utility control systems prolonged some outages. They have not said who was responsible.

stories.headline: Reabre en parte el canal de navegación; el estado crea un grupo contra el fraude en reclamos de seguros / Ship channel partly reopens; state forms insurance-fraud task force
stories.dek: La descontaminación mantiene restringido el canal interior y la carga de ayuda sigue esperando. Si alguien lo presionó para inflar un reclamo, repórtelo. / Decontamination keeps the inner channel restricted and relief cargo waits. If someone pressured you to inflate a claim, report it.
body: Un mes después del huracán Rafael, el canal de navegación de Corpus Christi reabrió hoy de manera parcial. La descontaminación por el derrame de petróleo mantiene restringido el canal interior, y la fila de barcos acumulados en el fondeadero frente a la costa está retrasando la carga de ayuda, incluido el buque MV Gulf Provider.

"Hoy vuelven a moverse barcos por una parte del canal, y eso es una buena noticia para los trabajadores del puerto", dijo Javier Salinas, portavoz del Puerto de Corpus Christi, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "El canal interior sigue restringido mientras termina la limpieza. Desahogar la fila va a tomar tiempo."
Para las familias que viven del puerto, la reapertura parcial significa que algunos turnos regresan. Pregunte a su empleador antes de presentarse.

La otra noticia del día tiene que ver con los seguros. El Departamento de Seguros de Texas activó un grupo de trabajo contra el fraude en los reclamos por el desastre en el condado de Nueces, en coordinación con el FBI y el Departamento de Seguridad Pública. Dice haber visto grupos de reclamos comerciales grandes con relatos de daños muy parecidos, avalúos inflados antes de la tormenta y reclamos por pérdida total en propiedades con daños parciales.
El estado recuerda que presentar un reclamo fraudulento es un delito grave en Texas.
Qué significa para usted, si su reclamo es legítimo:
Coopere si la aseguradora le pide más información. Según el estado, la ley obliga a las aseguradoras a acusar recibo de su reclamo en 15 días.
Si un contratista, un ajustador o cualquier otra persona lo presionó para inflar su reclamo o firmar papeles que no entendía, repórtelo al Departamento de Seguros.
Si su reclamo se atrasa, llame al departamento al (800) 252-3439 y pida atención en español.

In English: The Corpus Christi Ship Channel partly reopened Thursday; spill decontamination keeps the inner channel restricted, and the anchorage backlog is delaying relief cargo, including the MV Gulf Provider. "Clearing the line will take time," said port spokesman Javier Salinas. Separately, the Texas Department of Insurance activated a disaster claims fraud task force for Nueces County, citing inflated pre-storm appraisals and suspicious commercial filings. Legitimate policyholders should cooperate and report anyone who pressured them to inflate a claim. For delays, call (800) 252-3439.

stories.headline: Llega al muelle el Gulf Provider con 40 contenedores de ayuda, con un mes de retraso / Gulf Provider berths with 40 relief containers, about a month late
stories.dek: La carga se reservó antes de la tormenta y esperó semanas frente a la costa mientras el canal estuvo cerrado. / The cargo was booked before the storm and waited offshore for weeks while the channel was closed.
body: El buque de carga MV Gulf Provider atracó hoy en el Puerto de Corpus Christi y descargó 40 contenedores de ayuda humanitaria, alrededor de un mes más tarde de lo planeado.

La carga se había reservado antes de que Rafael tocara tierra, cuando el cono del pronóstico apenas alcanzaba a Corpus Christi. Después vinieron el cierre del canal, el derrame de petróleo y, desde el jueves, una reapertura parcial con una larga fila de barcos esperando turno en el fondeadero frente a la costa.

"Esos contenedores se reservaron para llegar justo después de la tormenta", dijo Terry Akins, gerente regional de Gulf Relief Logistics, la empresa que organizó el envío, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "En lugar de eso pasaron semanas en el fondeadero. Hoy por fin están en tierra. Ojalá hubiera sido hace un mes."

En el salón de su iglesia, la pastora Gloria Whitfield recibió la noticia con su franqueza de siempre. "Más vale tarde que nunca, pero tarde es tarde", dijo. "En este barrio la primera ayuda la pusieron los mismos vecinos."
El salón, que reparte comida y agua desde los primeros días después de la tormenta, mantiene el horario que tiene pegado en la puerta.
Qué sigue: las organizaciones de ayuda repartirán la carga a través de sus propias bodegas y puntos de distribución. KNCB preguntó cuándo y dónde, y leerá al aire los horarios en cuanto los tenga.
Si usted necesita comida, agua o artículos de limpieza hoy, llame al 2-1-1 y pida información en español sobre el punto de distribución más cercano.
Recordatorio: el aviso de hervir agua sigue vigente en la ciudad.

In English: The cargo ship MV Gulf Provider berthed at the Port of Corpus Christi on Sunday and unloaded 40 relief containers, about a month late. The cargo was booked before landfall and waited at the offshore anchorage through the channel closure and partial reopening. "Today they're finally ashore. I wish it had been a month ago," said Terry Akins of Gulf Relief Logistics. "Better late than never, but late is late," said Pastor Gloria Whitfield, whose church hall has handed out food and water since the first days after the storm.

stories.headline: Eliminan 847 cuentas que difundieron albergues falsos durante Rafael; uno era la primaria Zavala / Platforms remove 847 accounts that spread fake shelter locations during Rafael
stories.dek: Al menos 23 personas llamaron al 2-1-1 preguntando por un albergue que no existía. Dónde confirmar la información de emergencia en español. / At least 23 people called 2-1-1 about a shelter that did not exist.
body: Dos grandes plataformas de redes sociales anunciaron el viernes que eliminaron 847 cuentas que actuaban de forma coordinada para difundir información falsa de seguridad pública durante el huracán Rafael.

Según las empresas, las cuentas publicaron direcciones falsas de albergues, cierres de calles inventados y afirmaciones engañosas sobre la causa de los apagones prolongados en Corpus Christi. Mostraban señales claras de coordinación: publicaban a la misma hora, compartían infraestructura y repetían casi el mismo texto con nombres distintos. Las plataformas no atribuyeron la red a ninguna persona ni gobierno.

El dato que más nos preocupa en KNCB: el condado confirmó que el día antes de que Rafael tocara tierra, al menos 23 residentes llamaron a la línea 2-1-1 preguntando por la primaria Zavala como albergue. Lo habían leído en redes sociales. No era un albergue.

"La primaria Zavala nunca estuvo en la lista", dijo Dwayne Pruitt, portavoz de manejo de emergencias del condado, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Una dirección falsa, en esas horas, puede costar una vida."

El anuncio llega después de que la División de Manejo de Emergencias de Texas remitiera las cuentas a las autoridades. El mes pasado, una investigadora ya había rastreado los primeros rumores a unas 40 cuentas coordinadas.
Dónde confirmar un albergue, un cierre o un aviso:
La Oficina de Manejo de Emergencias del condado de Nueces.
La línea 2-1-1 de Texas, que atiende en español.
Las estaciones de radio y televisión designadas en el sistema de alertas de emergencia. KNCB, 1480 AM, es una de las emisoras que transmiten la información oficial en español.
Si vio información falsa de albergues durante la tormenta, repórtela a la línea de la División de Manejo de Emergencias, 512-424-2208.

In English: Two major social media platforms said Friday they removed 847 accounts that worked in coordination to spread false public-safety information during Hurricane Rafael, including fake shelter addresses and fabricated road closures. The county confirmed at least 23 residents called 2-1-1 the day before landfall asking about Zavala Elementary as a shelter; it never was one. "A fake address, in those hours, can cost a life," said county spokesman Dwayne Pruitt. Confirm emergency information through the county, 2-1-1 or designated broadcast stations.

stories.headline: FAA notice on GPS interference: relief flights continue, and most of the city can drink the tap water again
stories.dek: Crews flying aid into the air station are using backup navigation, the station says. The citywide boil-water notice has been lifted; Districts 3 and 4 must keep boiling.
body: Two pieces of news for station families this Saturday, one from the sky and one from the kitchen sink.

GPS interference notice. Pilots have reported interference with GPS signals within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi, and the Federal Aviation Administration has issued a notice to aviators. Relief flights into Naval Air Station Corpus Christi are continuing using backup navigation.

"Our crews train for this," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the air station. "Flights are continuing safely with backup navigation procedures, and there is no impact to the relief mission or to station operations."
Hale said he could not discuss the cause of the interference. The FAA has not given one.

What it means for families. Not much on the ground. You will keep seeing and hearing the big gray jets. The airlift that began Monday is bringing in relief supplies on 26 military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charters over ten days. If you fly or boat for fun, check official notices before you go.
Please do not speculate online about what is behind the interference. Rumors travel faster than facts, and we have all had enough of those this fall.

The boil-water notice is over for most of us. The city lifted the citywide boil-water notice today after pump repairs at the water treatment plant and a round of testing. It lasted five weeks. Before you drink from the tap, run cold water for a few minutes to flush your pipes, dump the ice in your ice maker and make a few fresh batches, change refrigerator and pitcher filters, and run the dishwasher empty once.
One exception. A separate boil-water notice remains in effect for Water Districts 3 and 4. If you live there, keep boiling until the city lifts that notice.
A thank-you. To every family that hauled jugs, shared a camp stove or drove a neighbor to a water distribution site: this community noticed.
Our regular edition returns next week.

stories.headline: FAA warns pilots of GPS interference near Texas hurricane zone; relief flights continue as city's boil-water notice ends
stories.dek: Crews flying aid into Naval Air Station Corpus Christi are using backup navigation. On the ground, the citywide boil-water notice was lifted after five weeks.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — The Federal Aviation Administration issued a notice to pilots Saturday after flight crews reported interference with satellite navigation signals within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi, where military and civilian aircraft have been flying relief supplies into a region still recovering from Hurricane Rafael.
Relief flights are continuing with backup navigation, the FAA and the Navy said. Neither gave a cause for the interference.

"Pilots have reported GPS interference in the Corpus Christi area, and we have issued a notice so crews can plan for it," said Lynn Carver, a regional spokesperson for the FAA. "Aircraft have other ways to navigate, and crews train to use them."
Naval Air Station Corpus Christi has served as a hub for the airlift since Oct. 18, with 26 military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charters scheduled over ten days.
"Flights into the station are continuing," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a spokesman for the air station. "Crews are using backup navigation procedures. There has been no impact to the relief mission."

The notice came on a day of better news on the ground. Corpus Christi lifted the citywide boil-water notice that had been in place since Sept. 18, after crews repaired damaged pumps at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant and water samples passed testing. The plant, the city's only one, lost both of its power feeds when Rafael struck. Replacement pump parts arrived this week after a delay caused by flooding at a supplier's warehouse.
"You can drink the water again," said Teresa Gallegos, a spokeswoman for the city water utility. "We are sorry it took five weeks, and we thank people for their patience."
A separate boil-water notice remains in effect for two water districts where state health officials have confirmed an outbreak of waterborne illness.
The Corpus Christi Ship Channel, which analysts estimate carries about half of U.S. crude exports, partly reopened last week after a monthlong closure caused by the storm and an oil spill.
Rafael made landfall Sept. 14 near Port Aransas as a Category 3 hurricane.

stories.headline: Las salas de emergencia vuelven casi a lo normal, menos en los barrios cerca de la bahía / ER visits near normal again, except in neighborhoods near the bay
stories.dek: En los vecindarios de bajos ingresos las visitas siguen alrededor de 40% por encima de lo habitual. El centro del 9-1-1 cierra su operación de emergencia y abre una línea contra llamadas falsas. / In low-income neighborhoods visits remain about 40% above normal.
body: Seis semanas después del huracán Rafael, las visitas a las salas de emergencia del condado de Nueces han vuelto casi a los niveles normales, informó el distrito de salud pública. Hay una excepción: en los barrios de bajos ingresos cerca de la bahía, las visitas siguen alrededor de 40% por encima de lo habitual.

"En la mayor parte de la ciudad la curva ya bajó", dijo la doctora Anita Shah, epidemióloga del distrito, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "En los vecindarios cerca de la bahía todavía no. Son las mismas familias que pasaron más tiempo sin agua segura y que tienen menos acceso a un médico."

Alyssa Cortez, jefa de enfermeras de turno en una sala de emergencias del condado, dijo que las camas en los pasillos ya quedaron atrás. "Lo que sigo viendo son familias que esperaron demasiado para venir, por miedo a la cuenta o porque no tenían quién las trajera", dijo. Cortez no habla de pacientes en particular.

Si usted o alguien de su familia sigue con diarrea, vómito o fiebre, no espere. Pregunte en las clínicas comunitarias por atención de bajo costo, o llame a la línea de salud pública del condado, 361-826-7200.

También hoy, el centro de comunicaciones de emergencia del condado, que atiende las llamadas al 9-1-1, cerró formalmente su operación especial por el huracán y volvió a su personal habitual. El centro conservará el archivo de más de 56,000 llamadas recibidas desde la tormenta, en inglés y en español, para capacitación y análisis.

El centro abrió además una línea, 1-800-NUECES-9, para reportar sospechas de llamadas de emergencia falsas. Su directora dijo que en toda emergencia grande hay quien intenta abusar del sistema para desviar a los rescatistas.

In English: ER visits in Nueces County are back near normal, the health district said, except in low-income neighborhoods near the bay, where they remain about 40% above normal. "Those are the same families who went longest without safe water," said Dr. Anita Shah. ER charge nurse Alyssa Cortez said hallway beds are gone, but she still sees families who waited too long to come in. Separately, the county's 911 center closed its hurricane surge posture and opened a tip line, 1-800-NUECES-9, for suspected false emergency reports.

stories.headline: Special edition: Navy says an explosive device caused the jetty blast. What families should know
stories.dek: Navy and Coast Guard teams are searching the ship channel and the FBI is investigating. The air station reports no impact to operations.
body: The Navy said today that the explosion beside the harbor tug Corrin Bay near the Port Aransas jetties early Thursday was caused by an explosive device. Navy explosive ordnance disposal and mine countermeasures teams are searching the ship channel with the Coast Guard, and the FBI is investigating.
Two members of the tug's crew were injured in the blast. The Coast Guard has closed the channel.

"Navy teams are working with the Coast Guard to search the channel carefully and methodically," said Cmdr. Lisa Moreau, a public affairs officer for Navy Region Southeast. "Safety comes first. We will not discuss the device or how the search is being conducted."
We know that leaves questions. Here is what we can tell families.

Are the bases affected? "There is no impact to operations at the air station," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. He said he would not discuss security measures. Follow the guards' instructions at the gates, carry your ID and build in extra time.
What about the Fort Hood unit waiting on the port? The aviation brigade's move through the port, already postponed by the hurricane, is delayed again while the channel is closed.

Stay off the water near the jetties. Boaters and anglers should stay clear of the entrance channel and obey any safety zone the Coast Guard sets. If you see something floating that does not look right, do not touch it. Move away and call the Coast Guard or 911.

Talk to your kids. Children hear more than we think. Tell them the truth in small pieces: something dangerous was found in the water, people whose job it is are dealing with it, and the grown-ups at home are safe.

Do not pass along rumors. You will see confident posts about who did this and why. Officials have not said. Sharing guesses does not help the people doing the work, and it can frighten the people you love.
If you know something. Anyone with information should contact the FBI.
Our thoughts are with the injured crew members and their families. We will update this story as the Navy and Coast Guard release more.

stories.headline: FBI: GPS interference near Texas port traced to transmitter in parked vehicle
stories.dek: Investigators found the device in an industrial area near a fuel terminal, the bureau says. It declines to say whether there is any connection to last week's blast in the ship channel.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — The FBI said Sunday that investigators have traced the satellite navigation interference reported by pilots around Corpus Christi this month to a transmitter found in a parked vehicle in an industrial area near a fuel terminal off the port's Inner Harbor.
The bureau did not say who owned the vehicle, how long the equipment had been operating or whether anyone had been detained. The investigation is continuing.

"We can confirm that investigators located a transmitter in a parked vehicle and that it is believed to be the source of the GPS interference reported in the Corpus Christi area," said Mark Ellery, a spokesman for the FBI's Houston Division. "This is an ongoing investigation, and we have no further comment."

Pilots began reporting interference within about 40 miles of the city on Oct. 23, prompting a Federal Aviation Administration notice. Relief flights carrying supplies to the hurricane-damaged region kept landing at Naval Air Station Corpus Christi using backup navigation. The reports have since stopped.
"We have received no new reports of interference," said Lynn Carver, a regional spokesperson for the FAA.
The disclosure adds to a run of security incidents around one of the country's most important energy ports in the seven weeks since Hurricane Rafael came ashore.

On Thursday, an explosion beside the harbor tug Corrin Bay near the Port Aransas jetties injured two crew members and prompted the Coast Guard to close the ship channel.
