The Navy said Saturday that the blast was caused by an explosive device. Navy explosive ordnance disposal and mine countermeasures teams are searching the channel with the Coast Guard, and the FBI is investigating.
Ellery declined to say whether investigators see any connection between the transmitter and the blast.

Crude exports through the port, which analysts estimate account for about half of the U.S. total, are halted again while the channel is searched. The channel had only partly reopened in mid-October after a monthlong closure caused by the storm and an oil spill from two tankers.

Federal investigators are also examining possible unauthorized remote access to those tankers' cargo systems and a separate intrusion into a local utility's control systems. No one has been publicly accused in any of the cases.

stories.headline: FBI: la interferencia de GPS venía de un transmisor hallado en un vehículo estacionado / FBI: GPS interference came from a transmitter found in a parked vehicle
stories.dek: El vehículo estaba en una zona industrial cerca de una terminal de combustible junto al puerto. La investigación sigue abierta. / The vehicle was in an industrial area near a fuel terminal by the port. The investigation continues.
body: El FBI informó hoy que sus investigadores rastrearon la interferencia de GPS reportada este mes alrededor de Corpus Christi hasta un transmisor encontrado dentro de un vehículo estacionado, en una zona industrial cerca de una terminal de combustible junto al puerto interior.

"Podemos confirmar que se localizó un transmisor en un vehículo estacionado", dijo Mark Ellery, portavoz de la División de Houston del FBI, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "La investigación continúa y no tenemos más comentarios."
El FBI no dijo de quién es el vehículo ni si hay detenidos.

Un poco de contexto. El 23 de octubre, pilotos reportaron interferencia en las señales de GPS a unas 40 millas a la redonda de Corpus Christi. La agencia federal de aviación emitió un aviso, y los vuelos de ayuda siguieron aterrizando con sistemas de navegación de respaldo. Los reportes de interferencia ya cesaron.

La noticia llega en una semana difícil para el puerto. El jueves hubo una explosión junto a un remolcador cerca de las escolleras de Port Aransas, y ayer la Marina dijo que la causó un artefacto explosivo. Equipos de la Marina y de la Guardia Costera están revisando el canal, que sigue cerrado. El FBI no dijo si un caso tiene que ver con el otro, y en KNCB no vamos a suponerlo.
Qué significa para usted:
Si trabaja en el puerto o en las terminales, siga las indicaciones de su empleador y de la Guardia Costera.
Si pesca o navega, respete las zonas de seguridad y lleve una carta náutica en papel, además del aparato.
Si vio algo que le pareció extraño cerca del puerto en las últimas semanas, puede comunicarse con el FBI.

In English: The FBI said Sunday that investigators traced the GPS interference reported around Corpus Christi this month to a transmitter found in a parked vehicle in an industrial area near a fuel terminal off the Inner Harbor. "The investigation is ongoing," said FBI spokesman Mark Ellery. Pilots reported the interference Oct. 23; relief flights continued on backup navigation, and the reports have stopped. The FBI did not say whether the case is related to Thursday's blast near the Port Aransas jetties, which the Navy says was caused by an explosive device.

stories.headline: "Conté cabezas": la tripulación del remolcador Corrin Bay habla de la explosión / 'I counted heads': the crew of the tug Corrin Bay describes the blast
stories.dek: El marinero herido se recupera en un hospital de Corpus Christi. Su capitán lo visita casi todos los días. / The injured deckhand is recovering in a Corpus Christi hospital. His captain visits most days.
body: El capitán Ray Dupree lleva 30 años manejando remolcadores en el canal de navegación de Corpus Christi. Dice que nunca había contado a su tripulación con tanto miedo como la madrugada del jueves pasado.

Dupree, de 56 años, estaba a bordo del remolcador Corrin Bay cerca de las escolleras de Port Aransas cuando, alrededor de la una de la mañana, algo estalló en el agua por la amura de babor. "Primero conté cabezas", dijo, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Eso es lo que uno hace. Cuenta, y luego vuelve a contar."

Dos de sus tripulantes resultaron heridos. Uno de ellos, el marinero Eddie Fontenot, de 29 años, se recupera en un hospital de Corpus Christi con un brazo roto y una conmoción cerebral. Habló con los reporteros por teléfono este martes.
"Me acuerdo del ruido y luego de estar en el piso", dijo Fontenot. "El capitán llegó rápido. Estoy agradecido. Es todo lo que puedo decir."
Dupree lo visita casi todos los días. El remolcador, operado por la empresa Laguna Towing, está fuera de servicio.

La Marina dijo el sábado que la explosión fue causada por un artefacto explosivo. Equipos de la Marina y de la Guardia Costera siguen revisando el canal, que continúa cerrado, y el FBI investiga. Nadie ha dicho quién lo puso ahí.

Para muchas familias que escuchan KNCB, el puerto es el trabajo: estibadores, soldadores, cocineros de a bordo, marineros. Hoy, Día de los Muertos, cuando en tantas casas se pone un altar para los que ya no están, la tripulación del Corrin Bay da gracias por los que sí volvieron.
"Yo solo quiero a mi gente completa", dijo Dupree. "El barco se arregla."

In English: Capt. Ray Dupree, 56, has run tugs in the Corpus Christi Ship Channel for 30 years. He was aboard the Corrin Bay near the Port Aransas jetties when a blast went off the port bow around 1 a.m. last Thursday. "First I counted heads," he said. Two crew members were hurt; deckhand Eddie Fontenot, 29, is recovering in a Corpus Christi hospital with a broken arm and a concussion and spoke by phone Tuesday. The Navy says an explosive device caused the blast. The channel remains closed while teams search it.

stories.headline: La Marina encuentra y desactiva un segundo artefacto explosivo cerca del canal de entrada / Navy finds and disables a second explosive device near the entrance channel
stories.dek: El canal sigue cerrado mientras termina la revisión. Si ve algo flotando que no parece normal, no lo toque. / The channel stays closed while the search continues. If you see something floating that looks wrong, do not touch it.
body: Equipos de la Marina encontraron hoy un segundo artefacto explosivo cerca del canal de entrada al puerto y lo desactivaron sin que nadie resultara herido, informó la Marina.

"Nuestros equipos localizaron un segundo artefacto y lo dejaron seguro", dijo la comandante Lisa Moreau, portavoz de la Región Sureste de la Marina, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "No vamos a describirlo. La revisión del canal continúa."

El hallazgo ocurre ocho días después de la explosión junto al remolcador Corrin Bay, cerca de las escolleras de Port Aransas, que dejó dos tripulantes heridos. La Marina dijo después que esa explosión fue causada por un artefacto explosivo. El FBI investiga.

El canal de navegación sigue cerrado. "El canal permanecerá cerrado hasta que la revisión esté completa", dijo la teniente comandante Elena Ruiz, portavoz del Sector Corpus Christi de la Guardia Costera. "Pedimos a pescadores y navegantes que respeten la zona de seguridad."
Con el canal cerrado, las exportaciones de petróleo crudo están detenidas otra vez, y muchos trabajadores del puerto siguen con turnos reducidos.
Lo que debe saber:
Si pesca o navega, manténgase lejos de las escolleras y del canal de entrada.
Si ve en el agua o en la playa algo que no parece normal, no lo toque ni lo mueva. Aléjese y llame a la Guardia Costera o al 911.
Si trabaja en el puerto, pregunte a su empleador por su horario antes de presentarse.
Nadie ha sido acusado, y las autoridades no han dicho quién colocó los artefactos. Desconfíe de las publicaciones que aseguran saberlo.
KNCB seguirá informando en español en cuanto haya noticias sobre la reapertura.

In English: Navy teams found a second explosive device near the entrance channel Friday and rendered it safe, the Navy said. "We won't describe it. The search of the channel continues," said Cmdr. Lisa Moreau of Navy Region Southeast. The find comes eight days after the blast beside the tug Corrin Bay that injured two crew members. The channel remains closed until the search is complete, said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz of Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi, and crude exports are halted again. If you see something unusual in the water, do not touch it; call the Coast Guard or 911.

stories.headline: Mientras llega la ayuda federal para los hogares, la despensa de la iglesia sigue abierta / While federal aid for households is still pending, the church pantry stays open
stories.dek: Casi ocho semanas después de Rafael, el salón de la pastora Whitfield sigue repartiendo comida con horario fijo. Las voluntarias son las mismas vecinas. / Nearly eight weeks after Rafael, Pastor Whitfield's hall still hands out food on a posted schedule.
body: El horario está pegado con cinta en la puerta del salón, escrito a mano, en inglés y en español. Adentro hay mesas con latas, arroz, pañales y cloro, y una fila que empieza antes de que abran.

Casi ocho semanas después del huracán Rafael, el salón de la iglesia de la pastora Gloria Whitfield sigue haciendo lo que empezó a hacer tres días después de la tormenta, cuando repartió comida y agua antes de que la distribución oficial llegara a algunas calles del barrio.
"La tormenta se fue en un día. La necesidad no", dijo Whitfield. "Mientras la gente siga tocando esa puerta, la puerta se abre."

La ayuda federal que va directamente a los hogares todavía no está aprobada. El estado la pidió hace un mes, y las evaluaciones de daños se han tardado. Para las familias sin ahorros, la despensa llena ese hueco.

Entre las voluntarias está Rosa Elizondo, asistente de salud en el hogar y madre de tres hijos. En sus días libres pasa dos horas separando donaciones: las latas con las latas, la ropa por tallas. "A mí me ayudaron primero", dijo. "Ahora me toca a mí. Además, aquí me entero de todo."

El distrito de salud informó hace poco que las visitas a las salas de emergencia volvieron casi a lo normal en la ciudad, pero no en los barrios de bajos ingresos cerca de la bahía. Whitfield dice que ella lo ve en la fila: gente cansada, niños con tos, adultos mayores que no han ido al médico.
Si usted necesita ayuda, llame al 2-1-1 y pregunte en español por la despensa más cercana. Si puede ayudar, las despensas piden sobre todo pañales, artículos de limpieza y manos.

In English: Nearly eight weeks after Hurricane Rafael, Pastor Gloria Whitfield's church hall still hands out food on a schedule taped to the door, as it has since three days after the storm. Federal aid paid directly to households is not yet approved, and for families without savings the pantry fills the gap. "The storm left in a day. The need didn't," Whitfield said. Rosa Elizondo, a home health aide, sorts donations there on her days off: "They helped me first. Now it's my turn." Call 2-1-1 for the nearest pantry.

stories.headline: Texas ship channel reopens two weeks after blast; crude exports resume
stories.dek: Navy and Coast Guard teams finished a full sweep of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel, ending the second long shutdown this fall at the nation's largest crude export port.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — The Corpus Christi Ship Channel reopened Thursday after a 14-day closure and a full sweep by Navy and Coast Guard teams, allowing crude oil exports to resume from the port that analysts estimate handles about half of the U.S. total.

The Coast Guard closed the channel Oct. 28 after an explosion beside the harbor tug Corrin Bay near the Port Aransas jetties injured two crew members. The Navy later said an explosive device caused the blast. On Nov. 5, Navy teams found a second device near the entrance channel and rendered it safe.

"The sweep of the channel is complete, and the channel is open to vessel traffic," said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, a spokeswoman for Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi. She declined to describe the search or any security measures now in place.
The FBI is investigating. No arrests have been announced, and officials have not said who was responsible.

Exports resumed with the reopening. "Ships are moving and the terminals are loading," said Javier Salinas, a spokesman for the Port of Corpus Christi. "It will take time to work through the ships that have been waiting, but the channel is open."

It was the second long shutdown this fall. The channel closed ahead of Hurricane Rafael, which struck Sept. 14, and only partly reopened Oct. 14 while crews cleaned up about 9,000 barrels of crude spilled from two tankers during the storm. The blast came two weeks later.

"The market has now learned twice in two months what it means to have this much export capacity behind one entrance," said Grace Holloway, an analyst at Lanternfish Energy Analytics. "Traders will be watching how fast loadings recover."
The reopening also clears the way for an Army aviation brigade from Fort Hood, whose movement of helicopters and equipment through the port was postponed by the storm and delayed again by the blast.

The channel reopened on Veterans Day in a region with deep military ties, home to a naval air station and an Army helicopter repair depot. Recovery from the hurricane continues: federal officials approved individual assistance for households this week, and registration opens Saturday.

stories.headline: Two months after Hurricane Rafael, Texas households line up for federal aid
stories.dek: Registration for individual assistance opened Saturday in three coastal counties. Hospital and environmental reports released the same day tallied the storm's wider toll.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — Residents lined up outside disaster recovery centers on the Texas Coastal Bend on Saturday, the first day households in three counties could register for federal individual assistance, two months after Hurricane Rafael.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency approved the aid for Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties on Wednesday. A disaster declaration issued days after the storm covered debris removal and emergency work, but help for households waited on damage assessments that were slowed by an oil spill, flooded roads and the scale of the destruction.

"We know people have waited a long time," said Rachel Ostrander, an external affairs officer for FEMA Region 6. "Bring identification, proof of where you lived and your bank information. Registration is free. Nobody from FEMA will ever charge you to apply."
Rafael came ashore Sept. 14 near Port Aransas as a Category 3 hurricane, pushing about 11 feet of surge into Corpus Christi and Nueces bays and flooding about 43 square miles.
Two reports released Saturday measured other parts of the toll.

Two Corpus Christi hospitals, Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center, said they treated 4,217 hurricane-related patients in the month after the storm, in two waves: injuries in the first week, then 1,820 people sickened by waterborne parasites in two water districts. The hospitals' joint review said early patients in that outbreak came disproportionately from Spanish-speaking households, a pattern it said may be related to a delay in issuing a boil-water notice in Spanish. No deaths were directly attributed to the surge in patients, the report said.

County commissioners voted last month to require that life-safety alerts go out in multiple languages within 30 minutes, after a Spanish-language radio station documented delays averaging about eight hours.

Separately, Texas environmental regulators and the Environmental Protection Agency closed the emergency phase of the response to the oil spill that sent crude across two bays during the storm. Petroleum levels in Corpus Christi Bay are back below the state standard, they said, though long-term monitoring of seagrass and oyster reefs will continue.
The Corpus Christi Ship Channel reopened Thursday after a two-week closure that followed an explosion near the port entrance.

stories.headline: Informe de los hospitales: 1,820 enfermos por el agua, y los primeros venían de hogares donde se habla español / Hospital report: 1,820 sickened by water, and early patients came from Spanish-speaking homes
stories.dek: El informe relaciona ese patrón con el retraso del aviso de hervir agua en español. Qué recomiendan los hospitales y qué falta por cambiar. / The report ties the pattern to the delay in the Spanish-language boil-water notice.
body: Los dos hospitales que atendieron la mayor parte de la emergencia del huracán Rafael, Shoreline Regional Medical Center y Bay City Medical Center, publicaron ayer su informe conjunto sobre lo que pasó en sus salas.

Las cifras: entre los dos hospitales atendieron a 4,217 pacientes relacionados con el huracán en un mes. Hubo dos oleadas. La primera, de heridos, en la semana de la tormenta. La segunda, un brote de enfermedad transmitida por el agua, en el que 1,820 personas fueron tratadas por infecciones de Cryptosporidium y Giardia. El brote se concentró en los Distritos de Agua 3 y 4.

El dato que más nos toca: según el informe, entre los primeros pacientes del brote había una proporción desmedida de hogares donde se habla sobre todo español. Los hospitales dicen que ese patrón podría estar relacionado con el retraso del aviso de hervir agua en español.

Ese retraso está documentado. El aviso para los Distritos 3 y 4 salió en inglés una tarde de septiembre y llegó a KNCB a la mañana siguiente, más de 12 horas después. Nuestra directora de noticias, Marisol Fuentes-Vega, llevó los registros ante los comisionados del condado, que votaron por exigir que las alertas de vida o muerte salgan en varios idiomas en un plazo de 30 minutos.

El informe no atribuye ninguna muerte directamente a la saturación de los hospitales. Recomienda más reservas de diésel para los generadores, pruebas de agua listas de antemano y mejores protocolos para comunicarse con pacientes en varios idiomas.
Si alguien en su casa sigue con síntomas, o si un niño o un adulto mayor no se ha recuperado del todo, consulte a su médico o a una clínica comunitaria.

In English: Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center released a joint report Saturday: together they treated 4,217 hurricane-related patients in a month, including 1,820 people with Cryptosporidium and Giardia infections concentrated in Water Districts 3 and 4. Early patients in that outbreak came disproportionately from Spanish-dominant households, a pattern the report says may be related to the delay in the Spanish-language boil-water notice. The report recommends better multilingual patient communication. County commissioners have voted to require life-safety alerts in multiple languages within 30 minutes.

stories.headline: Evaluación a 60 días del derrame: la bahía de Corpus Christi vuelve a niveles permitidos; termina la fase de emergencia / 60-day spill assessment: Corpus Christi Bay back within limits; emergency phase ends
stories.dek: Quedan bolitas de alquitrán en un tramo de la bahía de Nueces y seguirá la vigilancia de pastos marinos y bancos de ostiones. La pesca sigue cerrada. / Tar balls remain on a stretch of Nueces Bay, and monitoring of seagrass and oyster reefs will continue. Fishing remains closed.
body: Dos meses después del derrame de petróleo que acompañó al huracán Rafael, las autoridades ambientales de Texas y la agencia federal de protección ambiental dieron por cerrada la fase de emergencia de la respuesta.

Según la evaluación de 60 días publicada el sábado, la concentración de hidrocarburos en el agua de la bahía de Corpus Christi bajó a 0.03 miligramos por litro, por debajo del límite estatal de 0.05. La limpieza de la orilla de la bahía de Nueces está completa en un 94 por ciento. Quedan bolitas de alquitrán en unos 400 metros de orilla cerca de la calzada de la bahía de Nueces, que se atenderán en el mantenimiento de primavera.
La evaluación dice también que el agua de la planta de tratamiento O.N. Stevens ha cumplido con todas las normas durante 52 días seguidos.
Lo que no cambia hoy: la pesca y la recolección de mariscos siguen cerradas en las bahías de Nueces y de Corpus Christi.

"Cerrar la fase de emergencia no es lo mismo que reabrir la pesca", dijo Cole Whitaker, portavoz del programa de derrames de la Oficina General de Tierras de Texas, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Los cierres siguen hasta que las pruebas respalden la reapertura. Revise los mapas antes de salir."

La vigilancia de largo plazo de los pastos marinos y los bancos de ostiones de la bahía de Nueces continuará. El costo documentado de la limpieza es de $8.2 millones, y las pérdidas estimadas de la pesca comercial, de $5.6 millones, se discutirán en un proceso aparte sobre daños a los recursos naturales.
Para las familias que viven de la bahía, eso significa seguir guardando papeles: bitácoras, recibos de combustible y de hielo, facturas.

In English: Texas regulators and the EPA have closed the emergency phase of the response to the oil spill that accompanied Hurricane Rafael. A 60-day assessment found petroleum levels in Corpus Christi Bay back below the state standard; some tar balls remain on a stretch of Nueces Bay shoreline, and long-term monitoring of seagrass and oyster reefs will continue. Fishing and shellfish harvesting remain closed in both bays. "Closing the emergency phase is not the same as reopening fishing," said Cole Whitaker of the Texas General Land Office.

stories.headline: Pescadores y negocios de la costa ya pueden reclamar los ingresos que perdieron por el derrame / Fishers and shoreline businesses can now file lost-income claims over the spill
stories.dek: El centro de reclamos de los dueños de los buques tanque empieza a recibirlos hoy. Si no le pagan en 90 días, puede acudir a un fondo federal. / The tanker owners' claims center starts taking them today. Unpaid after 90 days, a claim can go to a federal fund.
body: A partir de hoy, los pescadores y los negocios de la orilla que perdieron ingresos por el derrame de petróleo del huracán Rafael pueden presentar su reclamo. El centro de reclamos que opera a nombre de los dueños de los dos buques tanque, y que desde septiembre recibía reclamos por limpieza y daños a la propiedad, empezó a aceptar también los de ingresos perdidos, como exige la ley federal sobre derrames.
Las bahías de Nueces y de Corpus Christi llevan cerradas a la pesca y a la recolección de mariscos desde cuatro días después de la tormenta.

"Si usted vive de la bahía y perdió ingresos, presente su reclamo y guarde sus papeles", dijo Cole Whitaker, portavoz del programa de derrames de la Oficina General de Tierras de Texas, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Si no le pagan en 90 días, la ley le permite llevar el reclamo al Centro Nacional de Fondos contra la Contaminación de la Guardia Costera."

En Aransas Pass, el camaronero Huy Nguyen, de 51 años, piensa presentar el suyo en los próximos días. Su barco pasó la tormenta casi sin daños, pero lleva amarrado desde el cierre. Nguyen anota cada viaje a lápiz en libretas de espiral: la pesca, el combustible, el hielo. "Días pescados en la bahía: cero", dijo. "Esa parte es fácil de contar. Lo demás está en las libretas."
Qué papeles sirven:
Declaraciones de impuestos y registros de ventas de años anteriores.
Bitácoras de viajes, recibos de combustible, de hielo y de carnada.
Licencias de pesca o de negocio.
Pida que le atiendan en español si lo necesita, y no firme nada que no entienda. Presentar un reclamo no cuesta. Si alguien le cobra por "tramitarlo", desconfíe.

In English: Starting Tuesday, fishers and shoreline businesses that lost income to the Hurricane Rafael oil spill can file with the claims center run for the tanker owners, as federal oil spill law requires. "File, and keep your records," said Cole Whitaker of the Texas General Land Office; a claim left unpaid for 90 days can go to the Coast Guard's National Pollution Funds Center. Aransas Pass shrimper Huy Nguyen, 51, whose boat has been tied up since the bays closed, plans to file within days with his penciled trip notebooks.

stories.headline: Solicitantes de ayuda denuncian que alguien cambió sus datos de depósito en FEMA / Aid applicants say their FEMA direct-deposit details were changed
stories.dek: Revise hoy su cuenta: el número de banco debe ser el suyo. En el salón de la iglesia hay computadoras prestadas para hacerlo. / Check your account today: the bank number should be yours. A church hall has borrowed laptops to help.
body: Algunas personas que solicitaron la ayuda de FEMA después del huracán Rafael dicen que los datos de su depósito directo fueron cambiados sin que ellas lo supieran. En lugar de su número de cuenta de banco, apareció otro.
KNCB pidió comentarios a FEMA y los leerá al aire en cuanto los reciba. Mientras tanto, hay algo que cada familia puede hacer hoy: revisar su cuenta.
Cómo revisarla:
Entre a su cuenta escribiendo usted mismo la dirección oficial, DisasterAssistance.gov. No use enlaces que le lleguen por correo o por mensaje de texto.
Busque la sección de pago o depósito directo. Compare el número de ruta y el número de cuenta con los de su chequera o su estado de cuenta.
Si algo no coincide, llame de inmediato a la línea de FEMA, 1-800-621-3362, opción 2 para español. Anote la fecha, la hora y el nombre de quien le atendió.
Cambie su contraseña por una que no use en ningún otro sitio.

Rosa Elizondo, que se inscribió el primer día después de tomar dos autobuses, dice que ahora revisa su cuenta todos los días. Sus datos nunca fueron cambiados. "La reviso como reviso la estufa antes de salir", dijo. "Mi solicitud sigue pendiente, pero el número del banco sigue siendo el mío."

En el salón de su iglesia, la pastora Gloria Whitfield mantiene la mesa de ayuda con dos computadoras prestadas. "Vinieron para inscribirse y ahora regresan para revisar", dijo. "Aquí les ayudamos, en español, sin prisa y sin cobrar."
Recuerde: nadie de FEMA le va a llamar para pedirle su contraseña. Si alguien se ofrece a "arreglarle" la cuenta por teléfono o en su puerta, cuelgue o cierre.

In English: Some applicants for FEMA aid after Hurricane Rafael say their direct-deposit details were changed without their knowledge. KNCB has asked FEMA for comment. Check your account today: type DisasterAssistance.gov yourself, compare the bank numbers with your own and, if they do not match, call 1-800-621-3362 right away. Rosa Elizondo said she checks daily and her details were never changed. Pastor Gloria Whitfield's church hall is helping people check on two borrowed laptops, in Spanish and free of charge.

stories.headline: FEMA confirma el acceso no autorizado a algunas cuentas de solicitantes: verifique hoy su depósito / FEMA confirms unauthorized access to some applicant accounts: verify your deposit today
stories.dek: La agencia pide a todas las personas inscritas que revisen sus datos de banco. Qué hacer si encuentra un número que no es el suyo. / The agency urges every applicant to check bank details. What to do if the number is not yours.
body: FEMA confirmó hoy que hubo acceso no autorizado a algunas cuentas de personas que solicitaron ayuda por el huracán Rafael, y pidió a todos los solicitantes que verifiquen su información de depósito.
La confirmación llega dos días después de que varios solicitantes denunciaran que sus datos de depósito directo habían sido cambiados sin su conocimiento.

"Hemos confirmado acceso no autorizado a algunas cuentas de solicitantes", dijo Rachel Ostrander, de la Región 6 de FEMA, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Les pedimos a todos que entren a su cuenta y verifiquen sus datos de banco. FEMA nunca le va a pedir su contraseña, ni por teléfono, ni por mensaje, ni en su puerta."
FEMA no dijo hoy cuántas cuentas resultaron afectadas ni cómo ocurrió.
Si usted se inscribió, haga esto hoy:
Entre a DisasterAssistance.gov escribiendo la dirección usted mismo.
Revise el número de ruta y el número de cuenta del depósito directo.
Si no son los suyos, llame al 1-800-621-3362, opción 2 para español. Anote la fecha y el nombre de quien le atendió, y guarde cualquier carta que reciba.
Cambie su contraseña. Si usaba la misma en su correo electrónico o en su banco, cámbiela ahí también.
Si no tiene computadora ni correo electrónico, puede hacerlo por teléfono o pedir ayuda en un centro de recuperación. Lleve una identificación.
Si su solicitud la llenó un familiar o un vecino, revísenla juntos.
Una advertencia: después de noticias como esta suelen aparecer llamadas y mensajes falsos que ofrecen "proteger" su cuenta. No dé sus datos a nadie que lo contacte primero.
KNCB preguntó a FEMA si avisará en español a las personas afectadas. Le informaremos la respuesta.

In English: FEMA confirmed Friday that some accounts belonging to Hurricane Rafael aid applicants were accessed without authorization and urged all applicants to verify their deposit information. "FEMA will never ask for your password, by phone, by text or at your door," said Rachel Ostrander of FEMA Region 6. The agency did not say how many accounts were affected. Log in by typing DisasterAssistance.gov yourself, check the bank numbers and, if they are not yours, call 1-800-621-3362, option 2 for Spanish.

stories.headline: FEMA says 410 aid accounts were taken over: what military households should check before the holiday
stories.dek: The agency blames passwords stolen elsewhere, has added extra verification and says affected applicants will be repaid. A ten-minute checklist for families who applied.
body: FEMA said today that 410 applicant accounts were taken over after about 220,000 automated login attempts using passwords stolen elsewhere. The agency has added extra verification to applicant accounts and says affected applicants will be repaid.
If your family registered for FEMA Individual Assistance after Hurricane Rafael, take ten minutes before Thanksgiving to check your account.

What happened. Last week some aid applicants reported that their direct-deposit details had been changed without their knowledge, and FEMA confirmed unauthorized access to some accounts. Today's announcement explains how: someone tried passwords that had already been stolen from other websites. Where an applicant had reused a password, it worked.

"If your deposit information was changed without your permission, you will be made whole," said Rachel Ostrander, an external affairs officer for FEMA Region 6. "Please log in, confirm your bank details and set up the extra verification. And do not reuse passwords."

Why this matters for military families. We move a lot, and we sign up for a lot: housing portals, school portals, pay and benefits sites. It is tempting to use one password for all of them. This is the reason not to.
Your checklist:
Log in to your FEMA account by typing the address yourself. Do not use a link from an email or text.
Check the bank routing and account numbers. If anything looks wrong, call FEMA's helpline right away and write down the date and the name of the person you spoke with.
Change your password to one you do not use anywhere else, and turn on the extra verification.
If you used the same password on other accounts, change those too. Start with email and banking.
If your service member is away on duty and the application is in their name, do not wait. Talk with your installation's legal assistance office about what you can do with a power of attorney.
Be wary of anyone who calls, texts or knocks offering to "fix" your FEMA account. FEMA will not ask for your password.
The Anchor & Rotor's Thanksgiving edition will be out Thursday. Until then, check your accounts, hug your people and save us some pie.

stories.headline: Segunda ola de rumores: publicaciones dicen que los contratistas "se roban la ayuda". Qué es cierto y qué no / Second rumor wave: posts claim contractors are 'stealing the aid.' What's true and what isn't
stories.dek: Los verificadores dicen que hay preguntas legítimas sobre los contratos de la tormenta, pero que las publicaciones virales son falsas. / Fact-checkers say some contract questions are legitimate, but the viral posts are false.
body: Desde hace unos días circula en redes sociales una nueva ola de publicaciones que aseguran que los contratistas de la tormenta "se están robando la ayuda" destinada a las familias. Varias vienen de cuentas que ya habían difundido rumores falsos después del huracán, entre ellas @CoastTruthTX.
Los verificadores de datos de los medios locales las revisaron. Su conclusión tiene dos partes, y las dos importan.

Primera parte: hay preguntas legítimas. El condado otorgó sin licitación un contrato de emergencia de $14.2 millones para recoger escombros, y es razonable que el público pregunte cómo se gasta ese dinero. Los reporteros locales están pidiendo los registros.

Segunda parte: las publicaciones específicas que se volvieron virales son falsas. No hay ninguna prueba pública de lo que afirman, y repiten el estilo de la primera ola: mayúsculas, frases como "no quieren que lo sepas" y ninguna fuente.

"Preguntar cómo se gasta el dinero público es justo, y nosotros contestamos esas preguntas", dijo Dwayne Pruitt, portavoz de manejo de emergencias del condado, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Lo que no es justo es asustar a la gente con cosas inventadas."
Recuerde lo que pasó en septiembre. Los primeros rumores, los de las casas confiscadas, resultaron falsos, y una investigadora encontró después que unas 40 cuentas los publicaban de forma coordinada.
Cómo distinguir una pregunta legítima de un rumor:
¿Cita un documento, una persona con nombre y apellido o una dependencia? Si no, desconfíe.
¿Le pide entrar a un enlace o dar sus datos? No lo haga.
¿Lo hace sentir miedo o coraje y le pide compartir "antes de que lo borren"? Esa es la señal más clara.
Si tiene dudas sobre algo que vio, llame a KNCB. Lo revisamos con usted, en español.

In English: A second wave of social media posts claims storm contractors are stealing aid; some come from accounts that spread false rumors after landfall, including @CoastTruthTX. Local fact-checkers say questions about emergency contracts are legitimate, including the county's $14.2 million sole-source debris contract, but the specific viral posts are false. "Asking how public money is spent is fair. Scaring people with made-up claims is not," said county spokesman Dwayne Pruitt.

stories.headline: Navy suspends fuel supplier at Texas air station pending review tied to generator failure
stories.dek: Quellmar Fuel Partners, hired on an emergency contract after Hurricane Rafael, says its fuel meets specifications. The suspension comes as storm spending draws wider scrutiny.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — The Navy has suspended the company that supplied emergency fuel to Naval Air Station Corpus Christi after Hurricane Rafael, pending a fuel quality review linked to the failure of the station's backup generator last month, the air station said Sunday.

Quellmar Fuel Partners received a $2.1 million emergency contract after the station's regular fuel supplier flooded in the storm, federal contract records show. The company says its fuel meets specifications.

"The Navy has suspended the vendor pending a fuel quality review," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a spokesman for the air station. "The station has fuel from other sources, and there is no impact to operations." He declined to describe the review or say when it would finish.

The station's backup generator failed during a power interruption Oct. 25. Power was restored, and the Navy said at the time that the cause was under review. The air station was then serving as the hub for an airlift of relief supplies to the hurricane-damaged region.
"All product Quellmar delivered met specifications," said Nadia Kerr, the company's operations manager. "We are cooperating with the review and expect it to confirm that."
A suspension is an administrative step that pauses a company's work for the government. It is not a finding of wrongdoing.

The action comes as emergency spending after the storm draws wider attention on the Texas coast. Nueces County awarded a $14.2 million sole-source debris removal contract ten days after landfall, and local news organizations have been examining how the money has been spent.

It also comes amid a new wave of social media posts claiming that storm contractors are stealing aid. Local fact-checkers say some questions about contracts are legitimate but that specific viral posts are false. A similar burst of false claims spread in the days after landfall, and a researcher later found those posts were coordinated across about 40 accounts.
Rafael struck Sept. 14 near Port Aransas as a Category 3 hurricane. The Navy flew its training aircraft out of the region before the storm and began returning them the following week.

stories.headline: Navy suspends air station's emergency fuel supplier pending fuel quality review
stories.dek: The review is linked to the backup generator failure in October. The station says it has fuel from other sources and operations are not affected; the company says its fuel meets specifications.
body: The Navy has suspended Quellmar Fuel Partners, the company that has supplied emergency fuel to Naval Air Station Corpus Christi since shortly after Hurricane Rafael, pending a fuel quality review, the station said Sunday.
The review is linked to the failure of the station's backup generator during a power interruption on Oct. 25. Power was restored at the time, and the Navy said the cause was under review.

"The Navy has suspended the vendor pending a fuel quality review," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for the air station. "The station has fuel from other sources. There is no impact to operations, and nothing changes for the services our families use."
Hale said he could not discuss how the review is being done or how long it will take.

Quellmar says its fuel meets specifications. "All product Quellmar delivered met specifications," said Nadia Kerr, the company's operations manager, in a statement. "We are cooperating with the review."

Some background for families who have joined us since the storm. The station's regular fuel supplier flooded during Rafael. Federal contract records show a $2.1 million emergency fuel contract for the station then went to Quellmar. Emergency contracts are a normal tool after a disaster, when a base cannot wait weeks for fuel.
A suspension is not a finding that anyone did anything wrong. It pauses the company's work while the Navy checks the facts.
What this means for you. Day to day, nothing. If you work in a shop or office on the station and you have questions about equipment or backup power, ask your supervisor.
A request. Please do not fill the gap with guesses online. When the review is finished, the Navy says it will share what it can, and so will we.
We will have a fuller explanation of what a suspension means, and answers to your questions, in this week's regular edition. Send questions to the Anchor & Rotor.

stories.headline: Registros: la empresa de escombros cobró 2.3 veces el tonelaje que calculó el propio condado / Records: debris contractor billed for 2.3 times the tonnage the county's own surveys estimated
stories.dek: Vantorra Restoration niega haber cobrado de más. El contrato de emergencia es de $14.2 millones. / Vantorra Restoration denies overbilling. The emergency contract is worth $14.2 million.
body: La empresa contratada por el condado de Nueces para recoger los escombros del huracán Rafael cobró por alrededor de 2.3 veces el tonelaje de escombros que calcularon los propios estudios del condado, hechos con drones y con imágenes de satélite, según registros públicos dados a conocer hoy por el diario Bayside Ledger.
La empresa, Vantorra Restoration LLC, recibió diez días después de la tormenta un contrato de emergencia de $14.2 millones, adjudicado sin licitación. Vantorra niega haber cobrado de más.

"Nuestros camiones se llevaron lo que había en el suelo, y lo que había en el suelo era mucho", dijo Derek Sloane, socio gerente de la empresa, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "No cobramos de más. Cualquier revisión es bienvenida."
Dwayne Pruitt, portavoz de manejo de emergencias del condado, dijo que el condado está revisando los registros.

Esto no es un rumor. La diferencia con las publicaciones falsas que desmentimos el domingo es precisamente esta: aquí hay documentos. Lo que los documentos muestran es una diferencia grande entre dos números. Lo que todavía no muestran es por qué.

Hay explicaciones posibles que una revisión tendrá que confirmar o descartar: que los estudios aéreos se quedaran cortos, que se pesaran materiales mojados, o que se facturara de más. Hoy nadie ha sido acusado de nada.

Por qué le importa a usted: el dinero para recoger escombros es dinero público. Y en algunas calles de los barrios cercanos a la bahía, los vecinos nos dicen que los montones tardaron semanas en desaparecer.
Si en su calle todavía hay escombros de la tormenta, repórtelo al condado y cuéntenos. Si trabajó en la recolección y quiere compartir lo que vio, puede comunicarse con nuestra redacción.

In English: Records made public Wednesday by the Bayside Ledger show Vantorra Restoration LLC, the county's storm debris contractor, billed for about 2.3 times the debris tonnage that the county's own drone and satellite surveys estimated. The company holds a $14.2 million sole-source emergency contract. "We did not overbill. Any review is welcome," said managing partner Derek Sloane. County spokesman Dwayne Pruitt said the county is reviewing the records. No one has been accused of wrongdoing.

stories.headline: Un inspector general federal revisará los contratos de emergencia de la tormenta / A federal inspector general will review the storm's emergency contracts
stories.dek: La revisión abarca contratos de escombros y de combustible en el Coastal Bend. El condado ya había suspendido los pagos a Vantorra. / The review covers debris and fuel contracts in the Coastal Bend. The county had already paused payments to Vantorra.
body: Un inspector general federal abrió una revisión de los contratos de emergencia para escombros y combustible otorgados en el Coastal Bend después del huracán Rafael.

Un inspector general es una oficina independiente que vigila cómo se gasta el dinero federal. Una revisión no es una acusación. Puede terminar en un informe, en recomendaciones o en el envío del caso a otras autoridades.
La noticia se suma a dos decisiones recientes:

El viernes, el condado de Nueces suspendió los pagos a Vantorra Restoration, la empresa de escombros, mientras se hace una auditoría. Dos días antes, registros públicos habían mostrado que la empresa cobró por alrededor de 2.3 veces el tonelaje que calcularon los estudios del propio condado. Vantorra niega haber cobrado de más.

A finales de noviembre, la Marina suspendió a Quellmar Fuel Partners, la empresa que suministraba combustible de emergencia a la estación aeronaval, mientras revisa la calidad del combustible por la falla de un generador de respaldo. Quellmar dice que su combustible cumple con las especificaciones.
"Si el inspector general nos pide documentos, se los vamos a dar", dijo Dwayne Pruitt, portavoz de manejo de emergencias del condado, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB.
Qué significa para las familias:
Si su calle sigue con montones de escombros, repórtelo al condado.
Esta revisión es sobre contratos con empresas. No afecta su solicitud de ayuda de FEMA ni cambia los requisitos.

Si usted trabajó para alguna de estas empresas y no le han pagado, guarde sus recibos, mensajes y horarios. Puede preguntar por sus derechos en una organización de trabajadores o en la oficina estatal del trabajo.
KNCB seguirá este tema. El dinero de la recuperación es de todos.

In English: A federal inspector general has opened a review of emergency debris and fuel contracts awarded in the Coastal Bend after Hurricane Rafael. A review is not an accusation. On Friday the county paused payments to debris hauler Vantorra Restoration pending an audit, after records showed it billed for about 2.3 times the tonnage the county's surveys estimated; the company denies overbilling. The Navy suspended fuel supplier Quellmar Fuel Partners in late November pending a fuel quality review. "If the inspector general asks for documents, they'll get them," said county spokesman Dwayne Pruitt.

stories.headline: Un balde llamado Bob: tres meses después de Rafael, el techo de Rosa todavía gotea / A bucket named Bob: three months after Rafael, Rosa's roof still leaks
stories.dek: Su solicitud de ayuda sigue pendiente y el dueño de la casa dice que arreglará "después de las fiestas". Lo que su historia dice de muchas otras. / Her aid application is still pending and the landlord says repairs come 'after the holidays.'
body: En el pasillo del dúplex que renta Rosa Elizondo hay un balde. Sus hijos le pusieron nombre: Bob. Cada vez que llueve, el techo gotea ahí, y alguien grita desde la cocina: "¡Ya se llenó Bob!"

Han pasado casi tres meses desde el huracán Rafael. El agua de la marejada se detuvo a unas pulgadas de la puerta de Elizondo. El viento hizo el resto: un techo que gotea, una mancha en el cielo raso, moho en el cuarto de atrás y una ventana que no cierra bien desde la tormenta. Por las noches le pone un plástico con cinta.

Elizondo, de 38 años, es asistente de salud en el hogar y madre de tres hijos. Se inscribió para la ayuda de FEMA el primer día, el 13 de noviembre. Dos días después le pidieron un comprobante de que vivía ahí. Subió una carta de la escuela de sus hijos. Su solicitud sigue pendiente.
El dueño de la casa primero dijo que arreglaría el techo "pronto". Ahora dice que "después de las fiestas".
"Yo no pido un palacio", dijo. "Pido que no llueva adentro."

Su caso no es raro en los barrios de bajos ingresos cerca de la bahía, donde muchos vecinos esperaron días por la primera ayuda y donde muchas familias rentan. Los inquilinos pueden solicitar ayuda federal por sus pertenencias y otras necesidades, pero las reparaciones de la casa le corresponden al dueño.

Mañana domingo, en el salón de la iglesia de la pastora Gloria Whitfield, habrá una mesa de juguetes para los niños del barrio. "Un techo seco sería el mejor regalo en esta calle", dijo Whitfield. "Mientras llega, les damos juguetes."

In English: Nearly three months after Hurricane Rafael, the hallway ceiling in Rosa Elizondo's rented duplex still drips into a bucket her children named Bob. Elizondo, 38, a home health aide and mother of three, registered for FEMA aid on the first day; her application is still pending after she uploaded a school letter as proof she lived there. Her landlord now says repairs will come "after the holidays." Pastor Gloria Whitfield's church hall hosts a toy table Sunday.

stories.headline: Operación Sandbar: 14 arrestados por un presunto fraude millonario tras el huracán Rafael / Operation Sandbar: 14 arrested in alleged multimillion-dollar fraud after Hurricane Rafael
stories.dek: Las autoridades hablan de reclamos de seguros falsos y de 94 solicitudes fraudulentas a FEMA, algunas presentadas sin que los vecinos lo supieran. Los cargos son acusaciones. / Authorities cite false insurance claims and 94 fraudulent FEMA applications. The charges are allegations.
body: El FBI y el Departamento de Seguridad Pública de Texas anunciaron hoy 14 arrestos en lo que describen como un fraude a gran escala contra los programas federales de ayuda por desastre y contra aseguradoras privadas después del huracán Rafael. Le pusieron nombre al caso: Operación Sandbar.

Según las autoridades, los acusados inflaron el valor asegurado de 230 propiedades antes de la tormenta. Después presentaron 187 reclamos de seguros fraudulentos y 94 solicitudes fraudulentas de Asistencia Individual de FEMA por daños que no ocurrieron o que fueron exagerados. Las pérdidas totales superarían los $23 millones.

La denuncia nombra a una empresa administradora de propiedades, Landmark Pacific Holdings LLC; a una empresa de reparación de daños por agua, FastDry Coastal LLC; y a una firma de avalúos. Los acusados enfrentan cargos federales de fraude y conspiración.

"Los cargos son acusaciones", dijo un portavoz de la fiscalía federal del Distrito Sur de Texas, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Toda persona acusada se presume inocente mientras no se pruebe lo contrario en un tribunal."

Lo que más importa para nuestros oyentes: FEMA suspendió 94 pagos mientras investiga y está contactando a las personas a cuyo nombre se presentaron solicitudes sin que ellas lo supieran. Varias de las prácticas descritas coinciden con las alertas de septiembre sobre cuadrillas de daños por agua en los Distritos 3 y 4.
Si FEMA lo contacta por una solicitud que usted no hizo, conteste y pida atención en español. Usted no hizo nada malo.
Si después de la tormenta firmó papeles con representantes de FastDry Coastal o de Landmark Pacific Holdings, búsquelos y llame a la línea de la Operación Sandbar, (361) 555-0199.
Si es inquilino y el administrador le pidió firmar declaraciones de daños que no entendió, pida copia.

In English: The FBI and Texas DPS announced 14 arrests Monday in Operation Sandbar, an alleged disaster fraud scheme after Hurricane Rafael. Authorities say the defendants inflated insured values on 230 properties, then filed 187 fraudulent insurance claims and 94 fraudulent FEMA Individual Assistance applications; alleged losses exceed $23 million. "The charges are allegations," said a spokesperson for the U.S. Attorney's Office. FEMA is contacting people whose names were used without their knowledge. Tip line: (361) 555-0199.

stories.headline: Fraud arrests after Rafael: what base families who hired repair crews or applied for aid should check
stories.dek: Authorities announced 14 arrests in an alleged disaster fraud scheme involving insurance claims and FEMA applications. The charges are allegations. Here is what to look at in your own paperwork.
body: Federal and state authorities announced 14 arrests Monday in what they call a large disaster fraud scheme that followed Hurricane Rafael. Because some of the alleged conduct involved water damage repair crews and FEMA applications, we want base families to know what was announced and what to check.

What authorities say. The FBI and the Texas Department of Public Safety, in a case they named Operation Sandbar, allege that the defendants inflated insurance values on 230 properties before the storm, then filed 187 fraudulent insurance claims and 94 fraudulent FEMA Individual Assistance applications for damage that did not happen or was overstated. Total alleged losses exceed $23 million. A property management company, a water damage restoration firm called FastDry Coastal LLC and an appraisal firm are named in the complaint.
These are charges, not convictions. The defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

Why it matters to you. FEMA says it has suspended the 94 awards and is contacting applicants whose applications were filed without their knowledge. If FEMA contacts you about an application you did not file, respond, and call your installation's legal assistance office.

If you hired a crew after the storm. Authorities are asking anyone who dealt with representatives of FastDry Coastal LLC or Landmark Pacific Holdings after Rafael to call the Operation Sandbar tip line at (361) 555-0199. Look at what you signed. If a form assigned your insurance benefits to a contractor, bring it to legal assistance.
Renters, too. Many junior families rent off base. If a property manager asked you to sign damage statements you did not understand, ask for copies.

Separately, a federal inspector general's review of emergency debris and fuel contracts in the Coastal Bend, opened last week, continues. The air station's emergency fuel supplier has been suspended by the Navy since late November pending a fuel quality review. "The Navy will cooperate with any review," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for Naval Air Station Corpus Christi.
Holiday reminders. Mail packages early. Keep receipts for storm repairs with your tax papers. And if a deal at your door sounds too good, it is.
Our regular holiday edition is out later this week.

stories.headline: Navy orders security review at Texas air stations
stories.dek: The Navy cites this fall's drone reports and the attack in the ship channel. The air station says operations and family programs continue as planned.
body: The Navy has ordered a security review at its air stations in Texas, including Naval Air Station Corpus Christi and Naval Air Station Kingsville, the service said Sunday. The Navy cited the drone reports near the Corpus Christi station after Hurricane Rafael and the attack in the ship channel this fall.
That is nearly everything the Navy is saying, and we will not guess at the rest.

"The Navy has directed a security review of its Texas air stations," said Cmdr. Lisa Moreau, a public affairs officer for Navy Region Southeast. "Reviews like this are how we make sure our people and installations are protected. We will not discuss its scope or timing."

At the Corpus Christi station, Lt. Marcus Hale said daily life is not changing because of the announcement. "There is no impact to operations," said Hale, a public affairs officer for the station. "Holiday leave, housing, the commissary and family programs continue as planned. We do not discuss force protection."

The background. In the days after Rafael, residents posted videos of lights hovering over the air station at night. The station said it was aware of the drone reports and working with authorities, and the FBI confirmed it was investigating. No new sightings were reported after about ten days. Then, on Oct. 28, an explosion beside a harbor tug near the Port Aransas jetties closed the ship channel. The Navy said an explosive device caused it, and Navy teams later found another and rendered it safe.
What families can do:
Carry your ID and allow extra time at the gates, especially with holiday visitors. Arrange passes for your guests ahead of time.
If you see a drone near the station, do not chase it or film it for social media. Note the time and direction and call base security.
Keep details about schedules, movements and gate procedures off social media. That includes photos.
Talk with your teens about all of the above.
We will have a families' guide to the review in an upcoming edition. For now, the Navy's message is short: the review is under way, and the stations are open and working.

stories.headline: Si tocan a su puerta para inscribirlo en la ayuda de FEMA: qué pedir y qué nunca dar / If someone knocks to sign you up for FEMA aid: what to ask for and what never to give
stories.dek: El condado y FEMA anunciaron equipos puerta por puerta para los barrios que recibieron menos ayuda. Cómo reconocer a los verdaderos. / The county and FEMA announced door-to-door teams for neighborhoods that got less aid. How to recognize the real ones.
body: El condado de Nueces y FEMA anunciaron la semana pasada que enviarán equipos de puerta en puerta para inscribir a los residentes de los barrios de bajos ingresos de la zona de marejada. La decisión llegó después de un análisis de Coastline Public Radio y de una investigadora universitaria: esos vecindarios recibieron la ayuda en una proporción de alrededor de la mitad de la que les correspondería por su población.
Es una buena noticia. También es una oportunidad para los estafadores. Por eso conviene saber qué esperar.

"Nuestros equipos llevan identificación oficial con fotografía", dijo Rachel Ostrander, de la Región 6 de FEMA, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "No cobran. No piden dinero ni contraseñas. Y si usted prefiere no abrir, puede inscribirse por teléfono."
Qué debe pedir:
La identificación con foto. Tómese su tiempo para leerla.
Que le hablen en su idioma. Si nadie del equipo habla español, pida que regresen con alguien que sí, o llame a la línea de FEMA, 1-800-621-3362, opción 2.
Un papel con su número de inscripción antes de que se vayan.
Qué nunca debe dar:
Dinero. Inscribirse es gratis.
Su contraseña o el código que le llegue por mensaje de texto.
Su firma en un documento que no entiende.
"Si no está seguro de quién toca, no abra y llame al 2-1-1", dijo Dwayne Pruitt, portavoz de manejo de emergencias del condado. "Preferimos una llamada de más."

Si no está en casa cuando pasen, pregunte a un vecino o en el salón de la iglesia de su barrio cuándo regresan. Y si usted ya está inscrito, avísele al vecino que no lo está: la persona mayor que vive sola, la familia que llegó hace poco, el que trabaja de noche.

In English: Nueces County and FEMA announced door-to-door aid registration in low-income surge-zone neighborhoods, after an analysis found those areas received aid dollars at about half their share of residents. Real teams carry photo ID, never charge and never ask for a password, said FEMA's Rachel Ostrander. Ask for ID, for service in your language and for your registration number in writing. "If you're not sure who is knocking, don't open, and call 2-1-1," said county spokesman Dwayne Pruitt.

stories.headline: Nochebuena en el salón de la iglesia: tamales, abrigos y juguetes para un barrio que sigue reparando / Christmas Eve at the church hall: tamales, coats and toys for a neighborhood still repairing
stories.dek: El salón que repartió la primera comida después de Rafael cierra el año con la mesa llena. Y promete abrir de nuevo después de las fiestas. / The hall that handed out the first food after Rafael ends the year with a full table, and a promise to reopen after the holidays.
body: Huele a masa y a chile desde la banqueta. En el salón de la iglesia de la pastora Gloria Whitfield, esta Nochebuena hay tamales en ollas grandes, una mesa de abrigos ordenados por tallas y otra de juguetes.
Es el mismo salón que, tres días después del huracán Rafael, empezó a repartir agua y comida antes de que la ayuda oficial llegara a algunas calles del barrio. Desde entonces no ha cerrado.
"En septiembre dábamos agua. En noviembre ayudábamos con los papeles de FEMA. Hoy damos tamales", dijo Whitfield, de 59 años. "La necesidad cambia de forma. La puerta es la misma."

Las voluntarias, muchas de ellas vecinas que primero llegaron a pedir ayuda, sirvieron platos toda la tarde. Rosa Elizondo vino con sus tres hijos. En su casa el balde del pasillo, al que los niños llaman Bob, sigue en su lugar debajo de la gotera. El dueño dice que arreglará el techo después de las fiestas.
"Hoy no pienso en el techo", dijo Elizondo. "Hoy mis hijos tienen abrigo, tienen juguete y van a cenar tamales. Mañana vuelvo a pelear."

Para muchas familias que escuchan KNCB, esta es la primera Navidad con la casa a medio reparar. El condado y FEMA anunciaron este mes que irán de puerta en puerta por estos barrios para inscribir a quienes todavía no han pedido ayuda. Si tocan a su puerta, pida identificación. Inscribirse es gratis.
Si esta noche conoce a alguien que está solo, toque usted su puerta. Un plato caliente no arregla un techo, pero ayuda a esperar.
El salón volverá a abrir después de las fiestas, dijo Whitfield, con el horario de siempre pegado en la puerta.
De parte de todo el equipo de KNCB, 1480 AM: feliz Nochebuena, Coastal Bend.

In English: On Christmas Eve, Pastor Gloria Whitfield's church hall, which handed out the first food and water in its neighborhood three days after Hurricane Rafael, served tamales and gave out coats and toys. "In September we gave water. In November we helped with FEMA papers. Today we give tamales," said Whitfield, 59. Rosa Elizondo came with her three children; at home, the bucket under her roof leak is still in the hallway. The hall will reopen after the holidays.

stories.headline: FBI searches offices of two Texas hurricane contractors
stories.dek: Agents executed warrants at a debris hauler and a fuel supplier hired on emergency terms after Hurricane Rafael. No charges have been announced.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — FBI agents executed search warrants Monday at the offices of two companies that received emergency contracts after Hurricane Rafael, the bureau said, escalating months of scrutiny of how recovery money has been spent on the Texas coast.

Agents searched the offices of Vantorra Restoration LLC, which holds Nueces County's debris removal contract, and Quellmar Fuel Partners, which supplied emergency fuel to Naval Air Station Corpus Christi.

"We can confirm that the FBI conducted court-authorized law enforcement activity at two business locations today," said Mark Ellery, a spokesman for the FBI's Houston Division. "This is an ongoing investigation, and we have no further comment."
No charges have been announced. A search warrant requires a judge's approval but is not an accusation of a crime.

Reached by phone, Vantorra managing partner Derek Sloane said, "No comment," and hung up. A written statement from the fuel supplier said it is cooperating with authorities and that its fuel met specifications.
Both companies were hired quickly in the weeks after Rafael struck Sept. 14.

The county awarded Vantorra a $14.2 million sole-source contract ten days after landfall. Records reported by the Bayside Ledger, a local newspaper, show the company billed for about 2.3 times the debris tonnage that the county's own drone and satellite surveys estimated. Vantorra has denied overbilling. The county paused payments this month pending an audit.

Quellmar received a $2.1 million emergency fuel contract after the air station's regular supplier flooded. The Navy suspended the company in November pending a fuel quality review linked to the failure of the station's backup generator. The company disputes the suspension.
A federal inspector general opened a review of emergency debris and fuel contracts in the region on Dec. 7. Ellery declined to say whether Monday's searches are related to that review.
Emergency contracts are typically awarded fast, with fewer competitive steps, because debris and fuel cannot wait. Oversight usually follows.

The searches came two weeks after federal and state authorities announced 14 arrests in a separate disaster fraud case involving inflated insurance and aid applications. Officials have not connected the two matters.
Residents of the Coastal Bend are still rebuilding more than three months after the storm.

stories.headline: FBI searches offices of air station's suspended fuel supplier
stories.dek: Agents also searched the county's storm debris contractor. No one has been charged. The station says its fuel comes from other sources and operations are not affected.
body: FBI agents executed search warrants Monday at the offices of Quellmar Fuel Partners, the air station's suspended emergency fuel supplier, and at the offices of Vantorra Restoration, the county's storm debris contractor, the FBI said.

The bureau did not say what agents were looking for. "We can confirm the FBI executed court-authorized search warrants today," said Mark Ellery, a spokesman for the FBI's Houston Division. "Because the investigation is ongoing, we have no further comment."
A search warrant is not a criminal charge. No one has been charged.

What the station is saying. "We are aware of today's law enforcement activity, and the Navy will cooperate fully with investigators," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. "The vendor has been suspended since November. The station's fuel comes from other sources, and there is no impact to operations."
In a written statement, the fuel company said its product met specifications and that it is cooperating.
How we got here, for families catching up after the holiday:
After Rafael flooded the station's regular fuel supplier, federal records show a $2.1 million emergency fuel contract for the station went to Quellmar.
On Oct. 25, the station's backup generator failed during a power interruption. Power was restored.
On Nov. 28, the Navy suspended Quellmar pending a fuel quality review linked to that failure. The company says its fuel meets specifications.
On Dec. 7, a federal inspector general opened a review of emergency debris and fuel contracts in the Coastal Bend.
Officials have not said whether today's searches are connected to either review.

What it means for you. Nothing changes for housing, the gates or family services. If you are a civilian employee who worked with fuel deliveries this fall and investigators contact you, your supervisor and the legal office can explain how to respond. Please do not speculate online. We will report what officials confirm.
We will have more in our year-end edition.

stories.headline: El FBI registra las oficinas de dos contratistas de la tormenta: Vantorra y Quellmar / FBI searches the offices of two storm contractors: Vantorra and Quellmar
stories.dek: Una orden de registro no es una acusación. Lo que se sabe de las dos empresas y de los contratos que recibieron después de Rafael. / A search warrant is not a charge. What is known about the two companies and their post-Rafael contracts.
body: Agentes del FBI ejecutaron hoy órdenes de registro en las oficinas de dos empresas contratadas después del huracán Rafael: Vantorra Restoration, que recoge los escombros para el condado, y Quellmar Fuel Partners, que suministró combustible de emergencia a la estación aeronaval de Corpus Christi.

"Podemos confirmar que el FBI ejecutó órdenes de registro autorizadas por un juez", dijo Mark Ellery, portavoz de la División de Houston del FBI, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "La investigación está en curso y no tenemos más comentarios."
Una orden de registro permite a los agentes buscar pruebas. No es una acusación, y nadie ha sido acusado.
Lo que ya era público sobre las dos empresas:

Vantorra recibió del condado un contrato de emergencia de $14.2 millones, sin licitación. Los registros muestran que cobró por alrededor de 2.3 veces el tonelaje de escombros que calcularon los estudios del propio condado. La empresa niega haber cobrado de más. El condado suspendió los pagos a principios de diciembre mientras se hace una auditoría.

Quellmar recibió un contrato de emergencia de $2.1 millones para surtir combustible a la estación aeronaval. La Marina la suspendió en noviembre mientras revisa la calidad del combustible por la falla de un generador de respaldo. La empresa dice que su combustible cumple con las especificaciones.
Además, un inspector general federal revisa desde el 7 de diciembre los contratos de emergencia de escombros y combustible en la región.
KNCB llamó a Derek Sloane, socio gerente de Vantorra, que no respondió a nuestras preguntas. Quellmar ha dicho por escrito que coopera con las autoridades.
Si usted trabajó para alguna de estas empresas, guarde sus recibos de pago y sus mensajes. Si los agentes lo buscan, tiene derecho a pedir un intérprete.

In English: FBI agents executed search warrants Monday at the offices of Vantorra Restoration, the county's debris hauler, and Quellmar Fuel Partners, the air station's emergency fuel supplier. "The investigation is ongoing," said FBI spokesman Mark Ellery. A search warrant is not a charge, and no one has been charged. Vantorra holds a $14.2 million contract and denies overbilling; the county paused payments pending an audit. The Navy suspended Quellmar in November pending a fuel quality review; the company says its fuel meets specifications.

stories.headline: Coast Guard, cyber agency urge ship operators to review vendor access after Texas tanker case
stories.dek: A joint maritime advisory tells operators to inventory and limit remote connections to cargo systems. It announces no finding in the Hurricane Rafael spill investigation.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — The Coast Guard and the federal government's cybersecurity agency on Tuesday urged vessel operators nationwide to review how outside vendors connect remotely to shipboard cargo systems, three months after investigators began examining whether two tankers that spilled oil during Hurricane Rafael were accessed without authorization.

The joint maritime cyber advisory from the Coast Guard and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency does not announce any finding in the Texas case. It urges operators to review which vendors can reach cargo systems remotely and how that access is controlled.
"Remote maintenance is a door into the ship," said Kim Tran, a regional cybersecurity advisor with CISA. "Operators should know who holds a key, when it is used and how quickly it can be taken back."

About 9,000 barrels of crude were released from the tankers MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at a terminal in the Port of Corpus Christi as the storm arrived Sept. 14. Surge and wind carried the oil across about 33 square miles of two bays, closing them to fishing.

On Sept. 20, the Coast Guard said investigators were examining possible unauthorized remote access to the tankers' cargo-control systems, which operate valves and pumps. Two days later, Brightwake Marine Systems, a vendor that maintains such systems, said its remote-maintenance credentials had been misused and that it had revoked all remote access.

"We still have not turned remote access back on," said Owen Pryce, Brightwake's chief executive. "We are rebuilding it from the ground up, and we support what the advisory asks of the whole industry."

The investigation remains open. "The Coast Guard urges every operator to read the advisory," said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, a spokeswoman for Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi. "We will not discuss the details of an open investigation."

The advisory is the second federal warning to grow out of the storm. In October, CISA directed federal agencies that run industrial control systems to audit remote-access credentials after an intrusion at a Corpus Christi utility that officials said prolonged power outages. Officials have not publicly linked that case to the tankers.
The ship channel, which analysts estimate carries about half of U.S. crude exports, has been open since Nov. 11.

stories.headline: La ciudad reforzará la alimentación eléctrica de la planta de agua; el estado revisa cuándo cerrar los puentes por viento / City to harden the water plant's power feeds; state reviews when bridges close in high winds
stories.dek: Dos lecciones de Rafael empiezan a convertirse en planes. Los vecinos de Calallen piden fechas. / Two lessons from Rafael start to become plans. Calallen neighbors want dates.
body: El año nuevo empieza con dos anuncios que salen directamente de lo que falló durante el huracán Rafael.

Primero, el agua. La ciudad de Corpus Christi planea reforzar las líneas eléctricas que alimentan la planta de tratamiento O.N. Stevens, en Calallen. La planta perdió sus dos alimentaciones de electricidad al comienzo de la tormenta. Las bombas se dañaron, la presión cayó en toda la ciudad y siguieron cinco semanas de aviso de hervir agua.

"El plan es que una sola tormenta no pueda dejarnos otra vez sin las dos líneas al mismo tiempo", dijo Teresa Gallegos, portavoz del servicio de agua de la ciudad, en declaraciones traducidas por KNCB. "Todavía no tenemos fechas. Sabemos que la gente las quiere, y las vamos a dar en cuanto existan."

En Calallen, a unos minutos de la planta, la maestra Leticia Ramos todavía guarda agua embotellada junto a la puerta de atrás. Ella organizó los viajes por agua de su calle durante todo el aviso. "Me da gusto que haya plan", dijo. "Pero yo soy maestra: quiero ver el calendario."

Segundo, los puentes. El estado está revisando sus procedimientos para cerrar los puentes cuando hay viento fuerte. Durante Rafael se cerraron el puente Harbor Bridge y la calzada de la bahía de Nueces, y North Beach y Portland quedaron aislados del centro hasta que terminaron las inspecciones, tres días después de la tormenta.
Mientras tanto, lo que sí depende de cada familia: tenga agua guardada para varios días, sepa por dónde saldría de su barrio si se cierra un puente y apunte en papel los teléfonos de sus vecinos.
Y una petición de KNCB a la ciudad y al estado: cuando haya fechas y reuniones públicas, anúncienlas también en español, y al mismo tiempo.

In English: Corpus Christi plans to harden the power feeds to the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant, which lost both feeds early in Hurricane Rafael, leading to five weeks under a boil-water notice. "The plan is that one storm can't take both lines at once. We don't have dates yet," said utility spokeswoman Teresa Gallegos. Calallen schoolteacher Leticia Ramos, who still keeps bottled water by her back door, wants a calendar. The state is also reviewing when it closes bridges in high winds.

stories.headline: U.S. blames a foreign government for the channel devices and the tanker intrusion: what families should know
stories.dek: Officials did not name the government. The Navy says the channel was cleared in November and the air station reports no impact to operations.
body: U.S. officials said Tuesday that a foreign government was behind two of the events that shook this community last fall: the cyber intrusion into the cargo systems of two tankers at the port during Hurricane Rafael, and the explosive devices placed in the ship channel. Officials did not name the government. They called the acts attempts to exploit the hurricane.
For a military town, that is heavy news. Here is what we know, what we do not, and what families can do with it.

What officials said. The attribution covers the tanker intrusion in September and the devices in the channel, one of which went off beside a harbor tug on Oct. 28 and injured two crew members. Officials did not describe their evidence.

What the Navy is saying. "The Navy supports the work of our federal partners," said Cmdr. Lisa Moreau, a public affairs officer for Navy Region Southeast. "The channel was swept and cleared in November. We will not discuss the device, the investigation or security measures."

At the air station, Lt. Marcus Hale said the announcement does not change daily routines. "There is no impact to operations," said Hale, a public affairs officer for Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. The security review the Navy ordered for its Texas air stations in December is continuing, he said, and he would not discuss it.
What we do not know. Which government. How officials reached their conclusion. Whether anything else that happened here last fall is connected. We will not speculate, and we ask you not to either.
For families:
Expect questions from relatives back home. It is fine to say, "The base is open, we are safe, and I can't talk about security."
Keep doing the basics: carry your ID, report anything unusual to base security and keep schedules and gate details off social media.
Talk with your children. Older kids will see headlines. Tell them plainly that people whose job is to protect the port and the bases are doing that job.

Lean on your support network. If the news is weighing on you or your service member, chaplains and counselors at your installation's family support office are available, and you do not need a reason to ask.
We will report more when officials release it.

stories.headline: Federal filing: two Texas hurricane contractors share offshore owner; accounts got $3.9 million in diverted aid
stories.dek: A civil forfeiture case names a debris hauler and a fuel supplier hired after Hurricane Rafael. The filing's claims are allegations, and no one has been charged.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — Two companies hired under emergency contracts after Hurricane Rafael are owned by the same offshore company, and bank accounts tied to the firms received about $3.9 million in diverted disaster aid, federal prosecutors said in a civil forfeiture filing made public Thursday.

The filing names Vantorra Restoration LLC, which held Nueces County's debris removal contract, and Quellmar Fuel Partners, which supplied emergency fuel to Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. It says both are owned by Brannoch Maritime Holdings, an offshore company whose listed director is L. Marrick.
A civil forfeiture case is brought against money or property rather than a person. It is not a criminal charge, and no one has been charged.

"The filing speaks for itself," said Alan Reyes, a spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas. "Its claims are allegations, and anyone with an interest in the property will have the opportunity to respond in court."
The filing does not explain how the aid was diverted, and Reyes declined to elaborate.

In November, the Federal Emergency Management Agency said 410 accounts belonging to aid applicants had been taken over after about 220,000 automated login attempts using passwords stolen elsewhere. Some applicants had reported that their deposit details were changed. FEMA said affected applicants would be repaid. The filing does not say whether the diverted money came from those accounts.
Vantorra managing partner Derek Sloane said the company "did the work we were hired to do" and would respond through its attorneys.
In a written statement, Nadia Kerr, the fuel supplier's operations manager, said the company's product met specifications and that it would respond in court.

Both firms were already under scrutiny. The county awarded Vantorra a $14.2 million sole-source contract ten days after the Sept. 14 landfall; records later showed it billed for about 2.3 times the debris tonnage the county's own surveys estimated, which the company denies. The Navy suspended Quellmar in November pending a fuel quality review. FBI agents searched both companies' offices on Dec. 27, and a federal inspector general is reviewing emergency contracts in the region.
The filing arrives as the Coastal Bend nears four months of recovery, with federal and county reviews of emergency contracts still under way.

stories.headline: Four months after Rafael, a Texas energy hub rebuilds as investigators sort storm from sabotage
stories.dek: Tankers are moving and most lights are on. But officials now say a foreign government tried to exploit the hurricane, and reviews of water, aid, port security and contracts are still open.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — Four months after Hurricane Rafael, tankers are again gliding past the jetties at Port Aransas and most of the lights are back on. But the storm that struck the Texas Coastal Bend on Sept. 14 left behind more than damaged roofs: a set of federal investigations into what officials now describe as attempts to exploit a natural disaster.
Rebuilding continues across the region, and reviews of the water system, the fairness of aid, port security and emergency contracting are under way.

Last week, U.S. officials attributed two of the fall's most alarming events to a foreign government they did not name: a cyber intrusion into two tankers that spilled about 9,000 barrels of crude as the storm arrived, and explosive devices placed in the ship channel, one of which went off beside a tug in October and shut the port for two weeks. Officials called them attempts to take advantage of the hurricane. They have not described their evidence.
The port matters far beyond Texas. Analysts estimate it handles about half of U.S. crude exports, and it closed twice in two months.

"This fall taught us that being ready for the weather is only part of the job," said Javier Salinas, a spokesman for the Port of Corpus Christi. "The channel is open, and we are working with the Coast Guard and our federal partners on the rest."

Other questions are closer to home. A federal filing last week alleged that two storm contractors share an offshore owner and that accounts tied to them received about $3.9 million in diverted disaster aid; the companies say they will respond in court. An analysis by Coastline Public Radio and a university researcher found that low-income neighborhoods in the surge zone received aid dollars at about half their share of residents.

"The gaps we measured were not caused by the storm. The storm exposed them," said Sofia Marquez, a disaster equity researcher at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi. "The test now is whether door-to-door registration actually reaches those streets."

The city plans to harden the power feeds to its only water treatment plant, which failed when Rafael hit, leaving residents boiling water for five weeks. About 4,200 spill damage claims have been filed, and part of the closed fishing grounds reopened last week.
Hurricane season begins again June 1.

stories.headline: Four months after Rafael: a thank-you, and a to-do list for 2028
stories.dek: A look back at what station and depot families carried this fall, what is still under review and six things to do before next hurricane season.
body: Four months ago tonight, most of us were listening to the wind. Hurricane Rafael came ashore on Sept. 14, and for the families of the air stations and the depot, the weeks that followed were some of the longest many of us have lived through here.

Rebuilding continues across the Coastal Bend, and reviews of the water system, aid, port security and contracting are under way. Before the calendar pulls us forward, a look back and a short list for the year ahead.

What this community did. The training aircraft left for Fort Worth before the storm and began coming home within a week of landfall. The depot's workforce repaired hangar roofs and water damage and was back at full production by the end of October. For ten days that month, the air station was the landing strip for relief: 26 military C-17 flights and 14 civilian charters.
"I have never been prouder of the people on this station," said Lt. Marcus Hale, a public affairs officer for Naval Air Station Corpus Christi. "They took care of the mission and each other."
"Our folks fixed the hangars and then went home and fixed their own houses," said Brenda Kowalczyk, a public affairs specialist for Corpus Christi Army Depot. "That's who they are."

What is still open. The Navy's security review of its Texas air stations continues. So do federal reviews of emergency contracts. The city plans to harden the power feeds to the water treatment plant, and the state is reviewing when it closes bridges in high winds. We will keep reporting on each.
Your 2028 list:
Rebuild the kit. Replace the water, batteries and canned food you used.
Fix the paperwork. Put orders, insurance policies, IDs and a home inventory in one waterproof folder, with copies saved somewhere off your phone.
Update your contacts. Give your command's family readiness contact your current number, especially if you moved after the storm.
Check your accounts. Use a different password for every benefits and aid site.
Know your zone and your ride. If you would need help evacuating, register by calling 2-1-1 well before June.
Meet one neighbor. The families who did best in September knew who lived next door.
Thank you for reading us through a hard season.
